docs.text:

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Highlights

  • Performance: faster editing of long roads, the references being only calculated again downstream of a modification, and faster calculation of the lines of the managed objects from their references
  • Road graph checks: new check G06 finding the previous and next edges inconsistent with the geometry, which give wrong references to the whole road. The checks are now numbered in the order of their fixes

Upgrade notes

  • Run the algorithm Upgrade database structure to upgrade the database (migration 45)
  • The checks G06 to G10 of the version 0.7.0 become G07 to G11, with their options

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • Road graph checks - G06: previous and next edges inconsistent with the geometry, which give a wrong order of the edges of the road and wrong references, fixed by setting them from the nodes (migration upgrade_to_45.sql)

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Road graph checks: the checks are numbered in the order of their fixes. The new check G06 is fixed after G05 and before the checks using the order of the edges: the checks G06 to G10 of the version 0.7.0 become G07 to G11. Their options set in the table glossary_graph_check are kept (migration upgrade_to_45.sql)
  • SQL: faster editing of long roads: after a modification of an edge or of a marker, the triggers only calculate again the references of the edges downstream of the modification, instead of all the edges of the road. For example on a road of 118 km with 135 edges: 1 s instead of 1.6 s for a vertex moved in the middle of the road, and 0.3 s near its end. The edges upstream are not rewritten anymore, which also lightens the editing sessions. The function update_edge_references has a new parameter _from_edge_ids (migration upgrade_to_45.sql)
  • SQL: faster calculation of the lines from their references (get_road_substring_from_references), for example for the managed objects with the update policy geometry: the parts of a line with an offset are ordered along the road with the order of the edges, instead of the references of their start and end points. The lines are the same, and a line with several parts is calculated 28 times faster: on the test data, 22 s instead of 48 s for 4,000 lines (migration upgrade_to_45.sql)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Highlights

  • Road graph checks: ten checks find the issues of the road graph, for example after an import: crossing edges without node, T junctions not connected, close nodes, useless nodes, reversed edges, roads with branches, parallel edges, short edges and markers issues. Most of them can be fixed automatically in an editing session, in batch or with a right click on the issue in QGIS (see the page Check and fix the road graph)
  • Edges and nodes: several fixes of the triggers keeping the road graph consistent when an edge is reversed, when an edge or a node is moved near another node, or when the end of an edge is moved

Upgrade notes

  • Run the algorithm Upgrade database structure to upgrade the database (migration 44). It repairs the edges whose geometry has been reversed without swapping their start and end nodes
  • After the upgrade, run the algorithm Check the road graph on the production schema to get an overview of the issues of the road graph, then fix them in an editing session

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Road graph checks: new algorithms Check the road graph and Fix the road graph issues, SQL functions check_graph and fix_graph_issue, and table glossary_graph_check listing the checks and their default options, to find the issues of the road graph, for example after an import, and fix them in an editing session (migration upgrade_to_44.sql)
  • Road graph checks: the layers created by the algorithm Check the road graph have actions to fix an issue with a right click (Fix this issue, Choose the fix of this issue…), or to select its edges, a style showing the fixed issues in grey, and the fields fix_status and fix_message storing the result of the fixes
  • Road graph checks - G01: edges crossing or touching each other without being split by a node. The edges touching each other are fixed by a node splitting them, and the edges crossing each other by a node or by the field no_intersection_cutting (bridge, tunnel), chosen for each issue
  • Road graph checks - G02: edges ending near another edge without being connected to it (T junction), fixed by extending the edge to the other edge, which is split there
  • Road graph checks - G03: nodes close to each other, fixed by merging them
  • Road graph checks - G04: useless nodes, without edge or between two edges of the same road, fixed by deleting the node, which merges the two edges
  • Road graph checks - G05: edges in the opposite direction of their road, found with the order of the markers or the direction of the neighbour edges, fixed by reversing them
  • Road graph checks - G06: roads with branches, i.e. more than two edges of the road at a node, for example ramps using the code of the road, to fix manually
  • Road graph checks - G07: parallel edges of the same road, for example two carriageways using the same road code, to fix manually
  • Road graph checks - G08: short edges, except near the roundabouts, fixed by removing the edge and merging its nodes
  • Road graph checks - G09: first marker of a road not at the start of the road, fixed by moving the marker to the start of the road when it is less than 1 m from it
  • Road graph checks - G10: markers not in the order of the road, far from the road, or on an edge without reference, to fix manually
  • Documentation: new page Check and fix the road graph, with a diagram of each check and of its fix

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Edges: when an edge is created or modified, its start and end points use the closest node less than 50 cm from them, instead of the node with the lowest id. Before, modifying any vertex of an edge could connect it to another node close to its start or end node
  • Edges: reversing the geometry of an edge, for example with the QGIS tool Reverse Line, now swaps its start and end nodes, and calculates again its previous and next edges and the references of its road. Before, the change was ignored, because the geometry was considered unchanged. The migration repairs the edges already reversed
  • Edges: when the end point of an edge is moved to another node, its old end node is deleted if no edge uses it anymore, like its old start node. Before, it was left without edge
  • Nodes: when a node is created or moved less than 50 cm from another node, the two nodes are merged, and the edge linking them, if any, is deleted. Before, this edge was left as a loop on the node

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Highlights

  • Managed objects: the split and merge of lines in Lizmap now give the right references, even for lines drawn in the opposite direction of the road, and the lines connected to an edited line stay connected
  • Security: the SECURITY DEFINER functions set their search_path, and the read-only functions work even if the search_path of the caller does not contain public

Upgrade notes

  • Run the algorithm Upgrade database structure to upgrade the database (migration 43)

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • SQL: new trigger function update_managed_object_linked_geometries: when the geometry of a managed line is updated, the lines of the same table and road which were connected to its start or end are shortened or extended to stay connected. Their references, and cumulative distances, follow the new references of the line, and their geometry is calculated again from them. The function add_managed_objects_triggers creates this trigger trg_update_managed_object_linked_geometries on the line tables, and now returns one line per trigger with its name (migration upgrade_to_43.sql)

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Lizmap: in the form Create the geometry from references of the editing panel, the fields Offset and Side are hidden by default: click on Offset to display them
  • Lizmap: the button Merge two lines of the popup no longer requires the right to delete features, but the rights to create features and modify the geometry. The editing rights needed to display the buttons Split a line at a point and Merge two lines can be changed with the new constants ROAD_SPLIT_NEEDED_RIGHTS and ROAD_MERGE_NEEDED_RIGHTS of the script road_network.js
  • SQL: merge of two managed object lines (Lizmap action merge_selected_lines): the merged feature is now the feature chosen first, with its field values, instead of the feature with the lowest start references. Its references, and its cumulative distances if the table has these fields, are calculated from the merged line in the direction of the road, even if the table has no trigger calculating them (migration upgrade_to_43.sql)
  • SQL: the functions called from outside the plugin which only read data (get_reference_from_point, get_road_point_from_reference, get_road_substring_from_references, get_managed_object_geometry_from_references, get_snapped_line_from_track, get_road_sections_from_snapped_line, get_spatial_road) and the trigger function calculate_managed_object_references now set their search_path to public: they work even if the search_path of the caller does not contain the schema public, where PostGIS is installed (migration upgrade_to_43.sql)
  • SQL: security: the SECURITY DEFINER functions copy_data_to_editing_session, drop_editing_session and toggle_foreign_key_constraints now set their search_path to public, pg_temp, and merge_editing_session_data prefixes the objects of the production schema (migration upgrade_to_43.sql)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• SQL: split of a managed object line by a point (Lizmap action split_line_by_point): for a line drawn in the opposite direction of the road, each part could get the references of the other part, or start after its end. The two parts now follow the direction of the road, like the geometries calculated from the references, and their four references, and their cumulative distances if the table has these fields, are calculated in the direction of the road (migration upgrade_to_43.sql)
  • SQL: the trigger calculating the references of the managed objects (trg_calculate_managed_object_references) gave a start reference greater than the end reference for a line drawn in the opposite direction of the road. They are now inverted, like in the algorithm Update managed objects from the road graph
  • Lizmap: in the form Create the geometry from references of the editing panel, the start and end references of a line drawn in the opposite direction of the road were displayed in the drawing order. They are now ordered in the direction of the road, like the geometry created from them

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Highlights

  • Performance: merging an editing session is much faster on long roads: only the managed objects which may be impacted by the modifications are updated, for example 0.4 s instead of 13 s for a new crossroad
  • Fixes: more precise cumulative distances (to the centimeter), and the managed lines are no longer shortened by 1 cm at each merge

Upgrade notes

  • Run the algorithm Upgrade database structure to upgrade the database (migration 42). It calculates again the references of all the edges, which can take a few minutes on a large road graph
  • Optionally, run the algorithm Update managed objects from the road graph on each managed table to correct their cumulative distances

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • SQL: faster merge of the editing sessions: only the managed objects which may be impacted by the modifications are updated (near the modified edges, downstream of them if the road geometry has changed, or near a modified marker), instead of all the objects of the modified roads. For example on a road of 118 km with 1,250 objects: 0.4 s instead of 13 s for a new crossroad, and 5 s instead of 13 s for a realigned edge (migration upgrade_to_42.sql)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• SQL: the cumulative distances greater than 10 km were rounded to 10 cm (1 m above 100 km), for the edges and the managed objects. The migration calculates again the references of all the edges (about 17 s for the 7,809 edges of the demo data). The managed objects are corrected when they are updated, or with the algorithm Update managed objects from the road graph
  • SQL: the managed lines with the update policy geometry were shortened by 1 cm at each merge
  • SQL: a managed object whose geometry cannot be calculated from its references no longer cancels the merge: it is not updated, and a warning is displayed
  • SQL: the list of the last updated managed objects (last_updated_objects_ids) is emptied when a merge does not update any object: it still contained the objects of the previous merge
  • Tools panel: the references displayed on click or on hover now show the marker 0, and the abscissa, offset or cumulative distance 0, instead of an empty field

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Highlights

  • Docs: new explanation of the impacts of the modifications on the references, with a diagram

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• SQL: faster editing of long roads: the references of a road are no longer calculated several times for one modification, and splitting an edge only calculates the references of its two parts. For example on a road of 135 edges, adding a crossing edge takes about 0.6 s instead of 8 to 13 s (migration upgrade_to_41.sql)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Highlights

  • GPS tracks: new Processing algorithm to get the road sections followed by the lines of a layer, for example GPS tracks, with their start and end references

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • Processing: new algorithm Get road sections from a line (GPS track) in the group Linear referencing, which snaps the lines of a layer, for example GPS tracks, on the road graph, and creates a layer with the sections of the roads they follow, with their start and end references

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• SQL: performance of the edges updates: the references of an updated edge are not calculated anymore by the trigger before_edge_insert_or_update when they are calculated again just after for the whole road, or when only another field of the edge has been modified. For example, modifying a field of all the edges of a road is a few hundred times faster (migration upgrade_to_40.sql)
  • SQL: new function road_graph.get_or_create_edge_node, used by the trigger before_edge_insert_or_update to get or create the start and end nodes of an edge, instead of duplicated code

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • SQL: the search of the next edge of an edge could fail if two edges of the same road started at the same node

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Highlights

  • GPS tracks: snap a GPS track, for example from a GPX file, on the road graph, and get the references of each road it follows (new SQL functions)
  • Performance: the calculation of the references is about 9 times faster for the edges, and about 3.5 times faster for the managed objects
  • Road graph editing: the field no_intersection_cutting is respected by all the trigger functions, drawing an edge across a highway interchange no longer hangs, and no orphan node is created anymore
  • Managed objects: new functions to add the reference fields and the triggers calculating the references, materialized view of the last updated objects, and fixed split of a line by a point in Lizmap
  • Documentation: reorganized and completed: Processing algorithms, tables and fields, functions examples, demo database, toolbar and panels, training plan

Upgrade notes

  • Run the algorithm Upgrade database structure to upgrade the database (migrations 31 to 39)
  • The editing schema editing_session is renamed road_graph_editing: recreate the QGIS administration project with the algorithm Create database local interface, or update the data sources of the existing projects
  • The Python code of the layer actions is now stored in the plugin: the plugin must be installed and activated to use the actions of the administration project

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• SQL: add the function road_graph.add_managed_object_reference_fields which adds to a managed object table the reference fields corresponding to its geometry type (migration upgrade_to_39.sql)
  • SQL: add the function road_graph.add_managed_objects_triggers() which creates the trigger trg_calculate_managed_object_references on every table listed in road_graph.managed_objects with the new column add_trigger_on_geom_change set to True, if it does not already exist
  • SQL: add the materialized view road_graph.vm_managed_objects, based on the view v_managed_objects and refreshed at the end of the function merge_editing_session_data. The QGIS administration project uses it instead of the view v_managed_objects
  • SQL: add the functions road_graph.get_snapped_line_from_track which snaps an imprecise GPS track (for example from a GPX file) on the road graph edges, without zigzags between close roads, and road_graph.get_road_sections_from_snapped_line which returns the ordered list of the roads followed by the snapped line, with their start and end references (migration upgrade_to_34.sql)
  • Docs: the Database menu now contains the pages Useful functions, which explains how to use these functions, and Database structure, which embeds the SchemaSpy documentation
  • Docs: explain the use of the field no_intersection_cutting in the page Road graph editing

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Docs: reorganization and new content of the documentation: new pages Processing algorithms and Tables and fields, description of the toolbar and panels of the plugin, examples of the linear referencing functions, creation of a demo database, example of the impacts of a graph modification on the business data, the preparation of the business tables moved to the page Managed objects, and a training plan in appendix
  • QGIS project: the Python code of the layer actions has been moved into the plugin (module roadnetwork/actions). The actions of the administration project now only call plugins['roadnetwork'].run_action(...): finalize_roundabout (layer edges copie), display_edited_data, create_editing_session and drop_editing_session (layer editing_sessions)
  • Processing: remove the Schema name parameter from the algorithms Create database structure and Upgrade database structure: the plugin schema is always road_graph
  • SQL: rename the editing schema editing_session to road_graph_editing (migration upgrade_to_32.sql). The table road_graph.editing_sessions and the functions *_editing_session* keep their names. The QGIS administration project and the plugin tools use the new schema name: QGIS projects created before must be recreated with the algorithm Create database local interface, or their data sources updated

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Processing: in the algorithm Update managed objects from the road graph, the option Preserve start & end points when updating line geometries had no effect
  • QGIS: in the panel RoadNetwork tools, pressing Enter in a field did not run the search Find
  • QGIS: the error message of the tool Get references under the cursor raised an error itself
  • Processing: the help of the algorithm Merge editing session data was the help of the algorithm cloning the data
  • SQL: the geometry of an editing session which status is not created could still be modified by setting its status back to created in the same query, or by removing it (migration upgrade_to_38.sql)
  • Lizmap: in the references form of the road network panel, the button Road of the start references went to the end of the road instead of its start
  • SQL: split of a managed object linestring by a point (Lizmap action split_line_by_point): the references were not updated when the table has no trigger calculating them. The first part now ends, and the second part starts, at the references of the cut point. A feature digitized in the opposite direction of the road can now also be split (migration upgrade_to_37.sql)
  • SQL: drawing an edge across edges crossing without node (bridges, highway interchanges) never ended: the parts of each split edge created nodes at all their intersections, which were propagated to the edges crossing them, and so on. Only the intersections of the drawn edge are now cut
  • SQL: when a new edge crossed several edges, a second node, not linked to any edge, could be created 10 cm away from a crossing node (rounding of the coordinates of the split parts)
  • SQL: the edges with no_intersection_cutting set to True were still cut by the nodes located on them, for example a new edge with this value passing over an existing crossroad. They are now only cut when the start or end point of a created or moved edge is located on them, for example a new access road arriving in the middle of a highway edge (migration upgrade_to_36.sql)
  • SQL: performance of the references calculation: the recalculation of the edges references of all the roads (update_edge_references) is about 9 times faster, with the same results. With the road cache, the previous marker is only searched among the markers of the road (all the markers of the database were read), and the edge order is stored in the cache instead of being calculated again for each point
  • SQL: performance of the update of the managed objects references (update_table_references_from_geometries), about 3.5 times faster on long roads: the road cache can now contain several roads, and is built for the roads of the objects before calculating their references
  • SQL: get_ordered_edges returned twice the edge of the roads having only one edge
  • SQL: when the first edge of a road is updated, for example when it is split by a new node, do not create a marker 0 if the road already has markers. Some roads do not start with the marker 0 (e.g. a road starting at the marker 4 + 918): a wrong marker 0 was created, or the editing failed with the error The object geometry must intersect the editing session polygon if the start of the road was outside the editing session (migration upgrade_to_33.sql)
  • SQL: the session variables road.graph.* used by the topology triggers are set with SET LOCAL, so that their value cannot leak outside of the current transaction (migration upgrade_to_33.sql)
  • SQL: remove the SET search_path / RESET search_path inside the functions drop_editing_session, editing_survey and split_edge_by_node, which now use the quoted schema name "road_graph". The function merge_editing_session_data has its search_path set in its definition
  • Locator: remove the prefix rr, which was ignored by QGIS (plugin prefixes must have at least 3 characters). The search is run without typing any prefix.

docs.title: Tags, publication, packaging
docs.text:
Tags and version numbers must follow SemVer convention.

To publish a new release, you must:

  • edit the pyproject.toml, change the version number and commit
  • add a new tag (it can be different that the version written in the file.)
  • push to Github (changes and tag)

Every tag pushed to Github will trigger a workflow dispach which will allow to create a Github release with a package for this version:

  • In the project Github repository, go to the tab Actions, menu Release, press the button Run workflows and check the needed options among:
  • Execute dry run
  • Publish to qgis.org then Run workflow

docs.title: Screenshots of the Processing algorithms
docs.text:
The screenshots of the Processing algorithm dialogs, used in the Installation and Import data pages, are generated automatically from the Python algorithms in roadnetwork/processing.

The script .docker/processing_screenshots.py opens each algorithm dialog in QGIS, without any display (Qt offscreen platform), in a temporary QGIS profile with a demo PostgreSQL connection named road_network_demo and the template layers of roadnetwork/resources/import. The images are saved in docs/media/installation and docs/media/user-guide.

To regenerate them locally, with the QGIS docker image (Docker is required):

make processing-screenshots
# Or with another QGIS version
make processing-screenshots QGIS_VERSION=3.40

To add a new algorithm, add its name and the output file name (relative to docs/media) in the ALGORITHMS dictionary of the script, then reference the image in the documentation.

The GitHub workflow .github/workflows/processing-screenshots.yml runs this command whenever the files in roadnetwork/processing are modified on the main branch, and opens a pull request if the screenshots have changed. It can also be run manually from the Actions tab.

docs.title: Translation of the documentation
docs.text:
The documentation is written in English and translated on Transifex, in the same project as the plugin interface. Each page is a resource named docs-<path of the page>, for example docs-user-guide-graph-checks, with the Markdown file format: Transifex splits it into strings (paragraphs, headings, list items, table cells), and keeps the translations of the strings which have not changed.

  • The English pages are sent to Transifex by the GitHub workflow .github/workflows/transifex.yml when the pages are modified on the main branch.
  • The translated pages are downloaded by the GitHub workflow .github/workflows/publish-doc.yml before building the documentation, every time it is published and every Monday. They are saved next to the English pages, with the language as suffix (graph-checks.fr.md), and are not versioned. The pages with less than 50 % of translated strings are displayed in English.
  • The MkDocs plugin mkdocs-static-i18n builds the site of each language (/fr/ for French), with a language selector. The titles of the menu are translated in mkdocs.yml (nav_translations).

  • The hook docs_tools/i18n_anchors.py gives to the headings of the translated pages the anchors of the English headings, so that the links to a section (graph-checks.md#g01-crossing-edges-without-node) work in every language.

  • The texts of the diagrams of the road graph checks are the resource docs-graph-checks-diagrams (key-value JSON file format). They are extracted by .docker/graph_checks_diagrams.py --extract, and the translated diagrams are written next to the English ones (graph_checks_g01.fr.svg, not versioned), mkdocs-static-i18n using them in the pages of the language.

The list of the translated pages is in docs_tools/transifex_docs.py. Translators must keep the Markdown syntax, the URLs of the links and the code unchanged.

To work locally, with the Transifex API token in the environment variable TRANSIFEX_TOKEN:

# Send the English pages
make doc-transifex-push
# Percentage of translated and reviewed strings of each page
make doc-transifex-status
# Download the translated pages, then display the site
make doc-transifex-pull
mkdocs serve

docs.title: Added

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Road graph checks: the checks are numbered in the order of their fixes. The new check G06 is fixed after G05 and before the checks using the order of the edges: the checks G06 to G10 of the version 0.7.0 become G07 to G11. Their options set in the table glossary_graph_check are kept (migration upgrade_to_45.sql)
  • SQL: faster editing of long roads: after a modification of an edge or of a marker, the triggers only calculate again the references of the edges downstream of the modification, instead of all the edges of the road. For example on a road of 118 km with 135 edges: 1 s instead of 1.6 s for a vertex moved in the middle of the road, and 0.3 s near its end. The edges upstream are not rewritten anymore, which also lightens the editing sessions. The function update_edge_references has a new parameter _from_edge_ids (migration upgrade_to_45.sql)
  • SQL: faster calculation of the lines from their references (get_road_substring_from_references), for example for the managed objects with the update policy geometry: the parts of a line with an offset are ordered along the road with the order of the edges, instead of the references of their start and end points. The lines are the same, and a line with several parts is calculated 28 times faster: on the test data, 22 s instead of 48 s for 4,000 lines (migration upgrade_to_45.sql)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Highlights

  • Road graph checks: ten checks find the issues of the road graph, for example after an import: crossing edges without node, T junctions not connected, close nodes, useless nodes, reversed edges, roads with branches, parallel edges, short edges and markers issues. Most of them can be fixed automatically in an editing session, in batch or with a right click on the issue in QGIS (see the page Check and fix the road graph)
  • Edges and nodes: several fixes of the triggers keeping the road graph consistent when an edge is reversed, when an edge or a node is moved near another node, or when the end of an edge is moved

Upgrade notes

  • Run the algorithm Upgrade database structure to upgrade the database (migration 44). It repairs the edges whose geometry has been reversed without swapping their start and end nodes
  • After the upgrade, run the algorithm Check the road graph on the production schema to get an overview of the issues of the road graph, then fix them in an editing session

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Road graph checks: new algorithms Check the road graph and Fix the road graph issues, SQL functions check_graph and fix_graph_issue, and table glossary_graph_check listing the checks and their default options, to find the issues of the road graph, for example after an import, and fix them in an editing session (migration upgrade_to_44.sql)
  • Road graph checks: the layers created by the algorithm Check the road graph have actions to fix an issue with a right click (Fix this issue, Choose the fix of this issue…), or to select its edges, a style showing the fixed issues in grey, and the fields fix_status and fix_message storing the result of the fixes
  • Road graph checks - G01: edges crossing or touching each other without being split by a node. The edges touching each other are fixed by a node splitting them, and the edges crossing each other by a node or by the field no_intersection_cutting (bridge, tunnel), chosen for each issue
  • Road graph checks - G02: edges ending near another edge without being connected to it (T junction), fixed by extending the edge to the other edge, which is split there
  • Road graph checks - G03: nodes close to each other, fixed by merging them
  • Road graph checks - G04: useless nodes, without edge or between two edges of the same road, fixed by deleting the node, which merges the two edges
  • Road graph checks - G05: edges in the opposite direction of their road, found with the order of the markers or the direction of the neighbour edges, fixed by reversing them
  • Road graph checks - G06: roads with branches, i.e. more than two edges of the road at a node, for example ramps using the code of the road, to fix manually
  • Road graph checks - G07: parallel edges of the same road, for example two carriageways using the same road code, to fix manually
  • Road graph checks - G08: short edges, except near the roundabouts, fixed by removing the edge and merging its nodes
  • Road graph checks - G09: first marker of a road not at the start of the road, fixed by moving the marker to the start of the road when it is less than 1 m from it
  • Road graph checks - G10: markers not in the order of the road, far from the road, or on an edge without reference, to fix manually
  • Documentation: new page Check and fix the road graph, with a diagram of each check and of its fix

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Edges: when an edge is created or modified, its start and end points use the closest node less than 50 cm from them, instead of the node with the lowest id. Before, modifying any vertex of an edge could connect it to another node close to its start or end node
  • Edges: reversing the geometry of an edge, for example with the QGIS tool Reverse Line, now swaps its start and end nodes, and calculates again its previous and next edges and the references of its road. Before, the change was ignored, because the geometry was considered unchanged. The migration repairs the edges already reversed
  • Edges: when the end point of an edge is moved to another node, its old end node is deleted if no edge uses it anymore, like its old start node. Before, it was left without edge
  • Nodes: when a node is created or moved less than 50 cm from another node, the two nodes are merged, and the edge linking them, if any, is deleted. Before, this edge was left as a loop on the node

Their references, and cumulative distances, follow the new references of the line, and their geometry is calculated again from them. The function add_managed_objects_triggers creates this trigger trg_update_managed_object_linked_geometries on the line tables, and now returns one line per trigger with its name (migration upgrade_to_43.sql)

  • SQL: the geometry of an editing session which status is not created could still be modified by setting its status back to created in the same query, or by removing it (migration upgrade_to_38.sql)
  • Lizmap: in the references form of the road network panel, the button Road of the start references went to the end of the road instead of its start
  • SQL: split of a managed object linestring by a point (Lizmap action split_line_by_point): the references were not updated when the table has no trigger calculating them. The first part now ends, and the second part starts, at the references of the cut point. A feature digitized in the opposite direction of the road can now also be split (migration upgrade_to_37.sql)
  • SQL: drawing an edge across edges crossing without node (bridges, highway interchanges) never ended: the parts of each split edge created nodes at all their intersections, which were propagated to the edges crossing them, and so on. Only the intersections of the drawn edge are now cut
  • SQL: when a new edge crossed several edges, a second node, not linked to any edge, could be created 10 cm away from a crossing node (rounding of the coordinates of the split parts)
  • SQL: the edges with no_intersection_cutting set to True were still cut by the nodes located on them, for example a new edge with this value passing over an existing crossroad. They are now only cut when the start or end point of a created or moved edge is located on them, for example a new access road arriving in the middle of a highway edge (migration upgrade_to_36.sql)
  • SQL: performance of the references calculation: the recalculation of the edges references of all the roads (update_edge_references) is about 9 times faster, with the same results. With the road cache, the previous marker is only searched among the markers of the road (all the markers of the database were read), and the edge order is stored in the cache instead of being calculated again for each point
  • SQL: performance of the update of the managed objects references (update_table_references_from_geometries), about 3.5 times faster on long roads: the road cache can now contain several roads, and is built for the roads of the objects before calculating their references
  • SQL: get_ordered_edges returned twice the edge of the roads having only one edge
  • SQL: when the first edge of a road is updated, for example when it is split by a new node, do not create a marker 0 if the road already has markers. Some roads do not start with the marker 0 (e.g. a road starting at the marker 4 + 918): a wrong marker 0 was created, or the editing failed with the error The object geometry must intersect the editing session polygon if the start of the road was outside the editing session (migration upgrade_to_33.sql)
  • SQL: the session variables road.graph.* used by the topology triggers are set with SET LOCAL, so that their value cannot leak outside of the current transaction (migration upgrade_to_33.sql)
  • SQL: remove the SET search_path / RESET search_path inside the functions drop_editing_session, editing_survey and split_edge_by_node, which now use the quoted schema name "road_graph". The function merge_editing_session_data has its search_path set in its definition
  • Locator: remove the prefix rr, which was ignored by QGIS (plugin prefixes must have at least 3 characters). The search is run without typing any prefix.

Every tag pushed to Github will trigger a workflow dispach which will allow to create a Github release with a package for this version:

docs.title: Screenshots of the Processing algorithms
docs.text:
The screenshots of the Processing algorithm dialogs, used in the Installation and Import data pages, are generated automatically from the Python algorithms in roadnetwork/processing.

The script .docker/processing_screenshots.py opens each algorithm dialog in QGIS, without any display (Qt offscreen platform), in a temporary QGIS profile with a demo PostgreSQL connection named road_network_demo and the template layers of roadnetwork/resources/import. The images are saved in docs/media/installation and docs/media/user-guide.

To regenerate them locally, with the QGIS docker image (Docker is required):

make processing-screenshots
# Or with another QGIS version
make processing-screenshots QGIS_VERSION=3.40

To add a new algorithm, add its name and the output file name (relative to docs/media) in the ALGORITHMS dictionary of the script, then reference the image in the documentation.

The GitHub workflow .github/workflows/processing-screenshots.yml runs this command whenever the files in roadnetwork/processing are modified on the main branch, and opens a pull request if the screenshots have changed. It can also be run manually from the Actions tab.

docs.title: Translation of the documentation
docs.text:
The documentation is written in English and translated on Transifex, in the same project as the plugin interface. Each page is a resource named docs-<path of the page>, for example docs-user-guide-graph-checks, with the Markdown file format: Transifex splits it into strings (paragraphs, headings, list items, table cells), and keeps the translations of the strings which have not changed.

  • The English pages are sent to Transifex by the GitHub workflow .github/workflows/transifex.yml when the pages are modified on the main branch.
  • The translated pages are downloaded by the GitHub workflow .github/workflows/publish-doc.yml before building the documentation, every time it is published and every Monday. They are saved next to the English pages, with the language as suffix (graph-checks.fr.md), and are not versioned. The pages with less than 50 % of translated strings are displayed in English.
  • The MkDocs plugin mkdocs-static-i18n builds the site of each language (/fr/ for French), with a language selector. The titles of the menu are translated in mkdocs.yml (nav_translations).

  • The hook docs_tools/i18n_anchors.py gives to the headings of the translated pages the anchors of the English headings, so that the links to a section (graph-checks.md#g01-crossing-edges-without-node) work in every language.

  • The texts of the diagrams of the road graph checks are the resource docs-graph-checks-diagrams (key-value JSON file format). They are extracted by .docker/graph_checks_diagrams.py --extract, and the translated diagrams are written next to the English ones (graph_checks_g01.fr.svg, not versioned), mkdocs-static-i18n using them in the pages of the language.

The list of the translated pages is in docs_tools/transifex_docs.py. Translators must keep the Markdown syntax, the URLs of the links and the code unchanged.

To work locally, with the Transifex API token in the environment variable TRANSIFEX_TOKEN:

# Send the English pages
make doc-transifex-push
# Percentage of translated and reviewed strings of each page
make doc-transifex-status
# Download the translated pages, then display the site
make doc-transifex-pull
mkdocs serve

docs.title: Presentation of the plugin concepts
docs.text: The RoadNetwork plugin helps to manage a topological county road network and to perform linear referencing with QGIS and PostGIS.

docs.title: Road network
docs.text:
Each road:

  • has an identification, e.g. D907,
  • is composed of a series of ordered edges (simple linestrings).

Markers are positioned along the roads. Their position is often measured with a GPS (X,Y).

docs.title: Topology
docs.text:
The road network is a graph built with edges and nodes:

  • each edge has a start node and an end node,
  • an edge can have a previous edge and a next edge,
  • intersecting edges are cut by a node (if they are on the same level).

docs.title: Position and references
docs.text:
This simple organization of roads, edges and markers allows to determine the position of any object based on:

  • a road code: D902,
  • a marker code: 1,
  • an abscissa: 500m.

You can also provide an optional offset, e.g. 3m, and a side, e.g. left.

Any point within a distance of 50m of any road will have its references: D902 PR 1 + 500m (3m left).

docs.title: Linear referencing
docs.text:
Each data object, point or (multi)linestring, is defined by its references calculated from the road network:

  • Points: trees, street lights, car accidents, etc.
  • Linestrings: paintings, safety barriers, roadworks, etc.

We must be able to:

  • calculate the references from the object geometry,
  • create a geometry based on given references:
    • a point,
    • a multi-linestring between two references.

docs.title: Corner cases
docs.text:
Discontinuity: edges could have been deleted (or have changed status).

Roundabouts have their own road code, e.g. GIR D35-D80, and cut the other roads.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Concept Definition Graph A directed graph made of a set of edges and nodes representing the road network as a road centerline network, matching the axis of the carriageway. Road A consecutive sequence of edges forming a road / a way (e.g. D115). Edge Portion of a road. An edge is a directed segment linking two nodes (simple line). Node The nodes represent the start and end vertices of each edge. Marker Point created by the road network manager, physically materialized on the ground by painted marks associated with kilometer markers. Virtual marker Point created by the GIS administrator to make the administration of the graph easier, especially the computation of the reference point + abscissa. Reference point (PR, point de repère) Formerly known as kilometer point. Business or thematic data Set of thematic data overlaid on the graph and topologically linked to it. It can be point data (e.g. road signs) or linear data (e.g. pavement surface).

docs.title: Useful functions
docs.text:
The road_graph schema provides SQL functions which can be used directly in your queries, for example in the QGIS Browser panel (right-click on the PostgreSQL connection or schema, then Execute SQL…), in psql or in a virtual layer built on a PostgreSQL query.

The examples below use the coordinate reference system EPSG:2154 and the road D613 of the test data of the plugin: the values can be slightly different in your database.

docs.title: Linear referencing functions
docs.text: Function Usage get_reference_from_point References of a point get_road_point_from_reference Point corresponding to references get_road_substring_from_references Line between two references get_spatial_road Geometry of a whole road, with the cumulative distances as measures

docs.title: Get the references of a point
docs.text:
road_graph.get_reference_from_point(_point, _road_code, _use_cache) returns the references of a point, as a JSON object:

SELECT road_graph.get_reference_from_point(
    ST_SetSRID(ST_MakePoint(473136.24, 6895774.58), 2154)
);

{
    "road_code": "D613", "marker_code": 44, "abscissa": 154.50,
    "cumulative": 43063.50, "offset": 15.00, "side": "left"
}
  • _point: the point, in the coordinate reference system of the road graph,
  • _road_code (optional): the code of the road to use. If it is not given, the closest road is used. Give it to choose the road of a point located near an intersection,
  • _use_cache (optional, False by default): used internally to speed up the calculation for many points of the same road.

The function returns NULL if no road is closer than 50 m from the point.

Example: get the references of all the features of a point layer, without storing them:

SELECT
    t.id,
    r.ref->>'road_code' AS road_code,
    (r.ref->>'marker_code')::integer AS marker_code,
    (r.ref->>'abscissa')::real AS abscissa
FROM managed.demo_trees AS t,
LATERAL (SELECT road_graph.get_reference_from_point(t.geom, t.road_code) AS ref) AS r;

docs.title: Get a point from references
docs.text:
road_graph.get_road_point_from_reference(_road_code, _marker_code, _abscissa, _offset, _side) returns the point corresponding to the given references, in the key geom of a JSON object (GeoJSON geometry):

SELECT road_graph.get_road_point_from_reference('D613', 44, 154.5, 15, 'left');

{
    "road_code": "D613", "marker_code": 44, "abscissa": 154.5, "offset": 15, "side": "left",
    "closest_marker_abscissa": 0,
    "geom": {"type": "Point", "coordinates": [473136.24, 6895774.58], "crs": {...}}
}
  • _offset: distance in meters from the road axis. Use 0 for a point on the road,
  • _side: left or right, in the direction of the road.

To get a PostGIS geometry:

SELECT ST_GeomFromGeoJSON(
    road_graph.get_road_point_from_reference('D613', 44, 154.5, 15, 'left')->>'geom'
) AS geom;

docs.title: Get a line between two references
docs.text:
road_graph.get_road_substring_from_references(_road_code, _start_marker_code, _start_marker_abscissa, _end_marker_code, _end_marker_abscissa, _offset, _side, _from_first_edge_start, _to_last_edge_end) returns the line of the road between two references, in the key geom of a JSON object:

-- Line of the road D613 between the references 44 + 100 m and 44 + 600 m
SELECT ST_Length(
    (road_graph.get_road_substring_from_references('D613', 44, 100, 44, 600, 0, 'right')->>'geom')::geometry
);
-- 500.00
  • the result is a MultiLineString: the road can be made of several parts, for example on both sides of a roundabout, which has its own road code,
  • _offset and _side: to shift the line from the road axis, e.g. 3 and left for a painting on the left side,
  • _from_first_edge_start and _to_last_edge_end (optional, False by default): extend the line to the start of the edge of the start references, and to the end of the edge of the end references,
  • the start references must be before the end references along the road, else an error is raised. If the start marker is before the first marker of the road, the line starts at the start of the road, and if the end marker is after the last marker, the line ends at the end of the road.

docs.title: Get the geometry of a road with measures
docs.text:
road_graph.get_spatial_road(_road_code) returns the geometry of the whole road, as a MultiLineString with measures (M): the measure of each vertex is its cumulative distance from the start of the road. It can be used with the PostGIS functions of linear referencing, for example ST_LocateAlong:

-- Point located 5000 m after the start of the road D613
SELECT ST_AsText(ST_LocateAlong(road_graph.get_spatial_road('D613'), 5000));
-- MULTIPOINT M ((507254.37 6896996.74 5000))

docs.title: Business data functions
docs.text:
These functions update the business tables listed in the managed_objects layer. They are described in the page Managed objects:

Function Usage update_table_references_from_geometries Calculate the references of the features of a table from their geometries update_table_geometries_from_references Calculate the geometries of the features of a table from their references (same page) add_managed_object_reference_fields Add the reference fields to a table add_managed_objects_triggers Create the triggers calculating the references automatically get_editing_session_impacts Get the impacts of an editing session on the roads, used by the merge to update only the impacted objects

docs.title: GPS tracks: from a GPX file to the road references
docs.text:
A GPS track recorded on the road, for example with a smartphone and exported as a GPX file, is never exactly on the road graph edges: the GPS precision is usually between 5 and 15 meters.

Two functions allow to transform such a track into road references:

  1. road_graph.get_snapped_line_from_track builds a line snapped on the road graph edges from the imprecise GPS track,
  2. road_graph.get_road_sections_from_snapped_line returns the ordered list of the roads followed by this line, with the start and end references (marker and abscissa) for each road.

Tip

Both steps can also be run on a whole layer of tracks in QGIS, without writing SQL, with the Processing algorithm Get road sections from a line (GPS track).

docs.title: Import the GPX file in PostgreSQL
docs.text:
A GPX file can be opened in QGIS with a drag & drop: choose the tracks layer. Then import it in the PostgreSQL database with the QGIS Browser panel: drag & drop the layer from the Layers panel onto the target schema of your PostgreSQL connection. The Processing algorithm Export to PostgreSQL can also be used.

The import can also be done with ogr2ogr:

ogr2ogr -f PostgreSQL PG:"service=my_service" my_track.gpx tracks \
  -nln gps.tracks -lco GEOMETRY_NAME=geom -lco FID=id

Tip

The tracks can stay in the GPS projection EPSG:4326: the functions reproject them automatically to the road graph projection. A geometry without SRID is considered to be already in the road graph projection.

docs.title: Snap the track on the road graph
docs.text:
SELECT road_graph.get_snapped_line_from_track(
    _track => t.geom,
    _densify_distance => 2,
    _max_distance => 25,
    _road_change_penalty => 100
) AS geom
FROM gps.tracks AS t
WHERE t.id = 1
;

Only the first parameter is required:

Parameter Default Description _track The GPS track: a linestring or a multilinestring, in any projection _densify_distance 2 Distance in meters between the points added to the track before snapping them _max_distance 25 The track points further than this distance (meters) from any edge are ignored _road_change_penalty 100 Penalty applied each time the road changes. Increase it if the result still has zigzags

The function returns a multilinestring in the road graph projection, which follows exactly the edges geometries, in the direction of the track.

In the example below, the GPS track and its points are displayed in cyan, and the snapped line in green. The track goes from the road D40 to the road D16 through the roundabout GIR_D40_D16-1:

Near the roundabout, the GPS track cuts the curves and crosses the roundabout, whereas the snapped line follows the edges of the 3 roads:

How does it work?

  • The track is densified with a point every _densify_distance meters.
  • For each point, all the roads closer than _max_distance are candidates.
  • Simply taking the closest road for each point would produce zigzags between two close roads (parallel roads, intersections, roundabouts). Instead, the function searches the sequence of roads which minimizes, for the whole track:
    • the distance between the points and their road (multiplied by _densify_distance, which gives approximately the surface in m² between the track and the roads),
    • plus _road_change_penalty each time the road changes between two consecutive points.
  • Each point is then snapped on the closest edge of its road. The small back and forth movements created near the intersections are removed.
  • If two consecutive edges are not connected, for example when a short roundabout section has been skipped, the gap is filled with the shortest path of maximum 5 edges. If no path is found, a new part is created in the multilinestring.
  • The result is built from the edges geometries, from node to node.

docs.title: Get the road sections references
docs.text:
SELECT s.*
FROM road_graph.get_road_sections_from_snapped_line(
    road_graph.get_snapped_line_from_track(
        ST_GeomFromText('LINESTRING(-0.044052 49.020203, -0.043663 49.019952, ...)', 4326)
    )
) AS s
;

The function returns one line per road section, ordered along the line:

road_order road_code start_marker start_abscissa start_cumulative end_marker end_abscissa end_cumulative direction length 1 D40 14 905.27 16361.8 15 396.15 16761.4 downstream 399.6 2 GIR_D40_D16-1 0 0 0 0 39.17 39.17 downstream 39.17 3 D16 0 716.82 716.82 0 1.62 1.62 upstream 715.19
  • start_marker & start_abscissa: the references of the section start, e.g. 14+905.27,
  • end_marker & end_abscissa: the references of the section end,
  • start_cumulative & end_cumulative: the distances from the road start,
  • direction: downstream if the line follows the road direction, upstream otherwise,
  • length: the section length in meters,
  • geom: the section geometry (linestring).

The second parameter _tolerance (default 1 meter) is the maximum distance between the line and the edges. The line must follow the road graph edges: use the result of get_snapped_line_from_track.

docs.title: Process all the tracks of a table
docs.text:
-- Snapped tracks
CREATE TABLE gps.snapped_tracks AS
SELECT
    t.id,
    road_graph.get_snapped_line_from_track(t.geom) AS geom
FROM gps.tracks AS t
;

-- Road sections of each track
CREATE TABLE gps.track_road_sections AS
SELECT
    st.id AS track_id,
    s.*
FROM gps.snapped_tracks AS st
CROSS JOIN LATERAL road_graph.get_road_sections_from_snapped_line(st.geom) AS s
ORDER BY st.id, s.road_order
;

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• A U-turn in the middle of an edge is not kept: the line leaves the edge by the node it came from.
  • With a very imprecise track (more than ~10 meters) in complex areas like highway interchanges, the result can contain wrong ramps, mainly at the track start or end. Increase _road_change_penalty, or cut the track ends.
  • The points further than _max_distance from the road graph are ignored. If the track leaves the road graph for a long distance, the result can be split into several parts.

docs.title: Database structure
docs.text:
The documentation of the road_graph schema (tables, views, columns, constraints, relationships and functions) is generated by SchemaSpy.

Open the database documentation in a new tab

docs.title: Tables and fields
docs.text:
The plugin stores the road graph in the PostgreSQL schema road_graph. The schema road_graph_editing has the same tables: it is the sandbox of the editing sessions.

This page describes the fields of the main tables. For the technical details (types, constraints, indexes, functions, etc.), see the Database structure.

The created_at and updated_at fields of the tables are filled automatically, and the uid fields contain a unique identifier (UUID) generated automatically.

docs.title: roads
docs.text:
The list of the roads. This table has no geometry: the geometry of a road is made of its edges.

Field Type Description id integer Unique identifier (automatic) road_code text Code of the road, e.g. D613. Unique. Used by the edges and the markers to refer to the road. road_type text road or roundabout. The roundabouts are managed differently by the trigger functions (see Create a roundabout). road_class text Class of the road: Départementale, Nationale, Autoroute, etc. It must exist in the table glossary_road_class. road_class_code text Code of the road class, e.g. the code of the French department is_active boolean If the road is active road_topic text Optional topic of the road, e.g. Port is_access_road boolean If the road is an access road

docs.title: edges
docs.text:
The edges of the road graph: each edge is a portion of a road between two nodes, drawn in the direction of the road.

Field Type Description id integer Unique identifier (automatic) road_code text Code of the road of the edge geom LineString Geometry of the edge. Its coordinates are rounded to 10 cm, except for the roundabouts. start_node integer Identifier of the start node (upstream node), filled automatically end_node integer Identifier of the end node (downstream node), filled automatically previous_edge_id integer Identifier of the previous edge of the same road, filled automatically if an edge of the same road ends at the start node. Empty for the first edge of the road. next_edge_id integer Identifier of the next edge of the same road. Empty for the last edge of the road. start_marker integer Code of the marker before the start point of the edge start_abscissa real Distance in meters between this marker and the start point start_cumulative real Cumulative distance in meters from the start of the road to the start point end_marker integer Code of the marker before the end point of the edge end_abscissa real Distance in meters between this marker and the end point end_cumulative real Cumulative distance in meters from the start of the road to the end point no_intersection_cutting boolean If True, the edge is not cut automatically at its intersections with the other edges, for example a bridge (see Edges which must not be cut). Default: False. id_source text Identifier of the edge in the source data, after an import

The references of the edges (start_marker, start_abscissa, start_cumulative, end_marker, end_abscissa and end_cumulative) are calculated automatically by the trigger functions each time an edge or a marker of the road is modified.

docs.title: nodes
docs.text:
The nodes of the road graph: the start and end points of the edges, and the intersections between the edges.

Field Type Description id integer Unique identifier (automatic) geom Point Geometry of the node. Two nodes cannot have the same geometry.

The nodes are created and deleted automatically by the trigger functions when the edges are edited. Creating or moving a node on an edge splits this edge.

docs.title: markers
docs.text:
The markers (reference points, PR in French) positioned along the roads.

Field Type Description id integer Unique identifier (automatic) road_code text Code of the road of the marker code integer Code of the marker, e.g. 12 for PR 12. Positive. abscissa real Abscissa of the marker in meters. 0 for a real marker, and the distance from the marker of the same code for a virtual marker, e.g. 613 for PR 72 + 613m. Positive. is_virtual boolean True for a virtual marker (PRV), created to make the administration of the graph easier geom Point Geometry of the marker id_source text Identifier of the marker in the source data, after an import

A road cannot have two markers with the same code and abscissa. A marker 0 is created automatically at the start of a new road, except for the roundabouts.

docs.title: glossary_road_class
docs.text:
The list of the road classes used by the field road_class of the table roads.

Field Type Description id integer Unique identifier (automatic) code text Code of the class, e.g. Départementale. Unique. label text Label of the class. Unique.

docs.title: editing_sessions
docs.text:
The editing sessions: the areas in which the road graph is edited in the sandbox (see Road graph editing).

Field Type Description id integer Unique identifier (automatic) label text Short label of the session author text Author of the session description text Description of the session geom Polygon Area of the session. It cannot be modified once the data has been cloned. status text Status of the session: created, cloned, edited unique_code text Code generated automatically with the creation date, e.g. editing_session_2026_10_28_08_37_24 cloned_ids jsonb Identifiers of the objects copied into the sandbox (roads, edges, nodes, markers) logged_ids jsonb Identifiers of the objects created, updated or deleted in the sandbox, used to merge the session

docs.title: managed_objects
docs.text:
The list of the business tables based on the road graph (see Managed objects).

Field Type Description id integer Unique identifier (automatic) schema_name text Schema of the business table table_name text Name of the business table. A table can be registered only once. geometry_type text Geometry type of the table: POINT, LINESTRING or MULTILINESTRING update_policy_on_graph_change text Update rule when the road graph changes: references (the geometry is kept and the references are updated) or geometry (the references are kept and the geometry is updated) add_trigger_on_geom_change boolean If True, the function road_graph.add_managed_objects_triggers() creates on the table the trigger calculating the references automatically. Default: False. last_update timestamp Date of the last update of the objects of the table last_updated_objects_ids integer[] Identifiers of the objects updated by the last update

docs.title: metadata
docs.text:
The version of the database structure, used by the plugin to know which upgrades must be run.

Field Type Description me_version text Version of the database structure me_version_date date Date of the version me_status integer Status of the version

docs.title: Views
docs.text: View Description v_road_without_zero_marker The roads which do not have a marker 0 v_managed_objects The objects of the business tables updated by the last merge of an editing session, as a 10 m buffer vm_managed_objects Materialized view of v_managed_objects, refreshed at the end of each merge (see Last updated objects)

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
To use the plugin, you need to:

  • install QGIS Desktop
  • install the plugin for QGIS
  • add a connection to a PostgreSQL database with PostGIS extension
  • install the database structure on this PostgreSQL database

docs.title: Get QGIS Desktop
docs.text:
The administrator must use the QGIS desktop software, version 3.40.x or above, to edit these needed metadata.

You can download QGIS in the official download page

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text:
At present, the plugin is not yet in QGIS official plugin repository. To install the plugin, you need to:

  • open QGIS Plugin manager (menu Plugins)
  • In the All tab, search for the word RoadNetwork and install the RoadNetwork plugin.

After a successful installation, you should see a new dock called RoadNetwork

For further details, you can have a look at 3liz documentation web page.

docs.title: Add a connection to the PostgreSQL database
docs.text:
The plugin stores all the data in a PostgreSQL database, with the PostGIS extension installed (to manage spatial data).

You need to have access to a PostgreSQL database, with enough rights to create a database schema and tables inside this schema.

In QGIS, use the Datasource manager under the Layer menu to create a new PostgreSQL connection:

  • Activate the PostgreSQL tab (elephant icon)
  • Click on the New button
  • In the creation dialog, fill the needed information, and use the Test connection button to make sure the credentials are ok.

We advise to:

  • use a service connection instead of the basic authentication. See QGIS documentation
  • check the boxes Use estimated table metadata and Also list tables with no geometry

Once your connection is set up, you can create the database structure in your PostgreSQL database

docs.title: Configure the plugin
docs.text:
This algorithm will allow to configure the extension for the current QGIS project.

You must run this script before any other script.

Parameters:

  • PostgreSQL connection to the database: name of the database connection you would like to use for the current QGIS project. This connection will be used for the other algorithms.

docs.title: Create the database structure
docs.text:
Install the database structure with tables and function on the chosen database connection.

This script will add a road_graph schema with needed tables and functions.

Parameters:

  • Connection to the PostgreSQL database: name of the database connection you would like to use for the installation.
  • Overwrite the database schema and all data ?: if the schema already exists in the database, the algorithm stops with an error, unless this box is checked. In this case, the existing schema is dropped with all its data and created again. Unchecked by default.
  • Geometry CRS: coordinate reference system of the geometries stored in the database. It must be a valid EPSG code. Default: EPSG:2154 - RGF93 v1 / Lambert-93.

docs.title: Upgrade database structure
docs.text:
Upgrade the tables and functions in the chosen database.

If you have upgraded your QGIS plugin, you can run this script to upgrade your database to the new plugin version.

Parameters:

  • Connection to the PostgreSQL database: name of the database connection you would like to use for the upgrade.
  • Check this box to upgrade. No action will be done otherwise: safety checkbox. The algorithm refuses to run if it is not checked.

The coordinate reference system is not asked: it is read from the existing edges table.

docs.title: Create your database local interface
docs.text:
This algorithm will create a new QGIS project file for administration purpose.

The generated QGIS project must then be opened by the administrator to edit the road network data by using QGIS editing capabilities

Parameters:

  • Connection to the PostgreSQL database: name of the database connection you would like to use for the new QGIS project.
  • Geometry CRS: coordinate reference system of the QGIS project and its layers. Use the same CRS as the one chosen when creating the database structure. Default: EPSG:2154 - RGF93 v1 / Lambert-93.
  • QGIS project file to create: choose the output file destination. We advise you to choose a name reflecting the database name.

You can then open the generated QGIS project.

docs.title: Lizmap Web Client tools
docs.text:
The road network can be published with Lizmap Web Client (LWC). A JavaScript script, road_network.js, adds tools to the web map so that users can work with linear references (road, marker, abscissa, offset and side) directly in the browser.

These tools rely on Lizmap actions: each tool calls a named action, which runs the PostgreSQL function lizmap_get_data(json). This function calls the road_graph functions of the plugin and returns the result as GeoJSON.

Note

The user interface is written in English and can be translated. This page gives the labels of the French interface, with the English text.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
The script adds four tools:

Tool Where Lizmap actions used Road network panel Mini-dock Graphe routier get_references_from_point, get_road_point_from_reference Create a geometry from references Editing form get_references_from_point, get_road_point_from_reference, get_road_substring_from_references, get_edge_start_or_end_tip_from_references Split a line Feature popup split_line_by_point Merge two lines Feature popup merge_selected_lines

docs.title: Road network panel
docs.text:
The script adds a mini-dock named Graphe routier (Road network). It opens when the map loads.

The panel contains a form with these fields:

Label Meaning Route Road code, for example D1. The list of values comes from the roads layer. PR Marker code (in French: point de repère) Abscisse Abscissa: distance in meters from the marker Cumul Cumulative distance in meters from the start of the road (read-only) Décalage Offset: distance in meters from the road axis Côté Side of the road: Gauche (left) or Droite (right)

docs.title: Get the references of a point
docs.text: When the panel is open, click on the map. The script runs the action get_references_from_point with the clicked point. The returned references fill the form, and the point is displayed on the map.

docs.title: Show the references when hovering the map
docs.text:
Check Activer le calcul au survol (Enable calculation on hover). When the mouse moves over the map, a tooltip displays the references of the point under the cursor, for example D1 - PR 3 + 250m (2m G). The values in the form are updated too.

To limit the number of requests to the server:

  • the script sends at most one request every 200 ms,
  • no request is sent while the user drags the map.

This option is not available while the editing form is open.

docs.title: Center the map on references
docs.text:
Type a road, a marker, an abscissa, an offset and a side in the form, then click Centrer (Center). The script runs the action get_road_point_from_reference and centers the map on the returned point.

Tip

Click and hover only work at scale 1:50,000 or larger. At a smaller scale, a message asks the user to zoom in.

docs.title: Create a geometry from references
docs.text:
When the user opens the Lizmap editing form for a point or line layer, the script adds a collapsible section above the form: Create the geometry from references.

The fields depend on the geometry type of the layer:

  • Point layer: road, marker, abscissa, offset and side.
  • Line layer: road, start marker and abscissa (PR début, Abscisse début), end marker and abscissa (PR fin, Abscisse fin), offset and side.

If the editing form has a field named road_code, its value is copied into the Route field.

docs.title: Buttons
docs.text:
Button Action Create Computes the geometry from the references and replaces the geometry of the edited feature. For a point layer, the script runs get_road_point_from_reference. For a line layer, it runs get_road_substring_from_references. If the start references are after the end references, the script swaps them. Reset Deletes the drawn geometry and resets the reference fields. Edge, start row Sets the start references to the start of the edge located at the start references. Road, start row Sets the start references to the start of the road. Edge, end row Sets the end references to the end of the edge located at the end references. Road, end row Sets the end references to the end of the road.

The Tronçon and Route buttons are only available for line layers. They run the action get_edge_start_or_end_tip_from_references. After that, the line geometry is computed again.

docs.title: Snap a drawn geometry to the road
docs.text:
When the user draws or modifies the geometry with the Lizmap drawing tools, the script:

  1. runs get_references_from_point for the point, or for the first and last vertices of the line,
  2. fills the reference fields with the returned values,
  3. replaces the drawn geometry with the geometry computed from these references.

As a result, the geometry always follows the road. If the road field has a value, only this road is used to find the references.

If no reference is found after 2 seconds, a message tells the user that the geometry could not be created. The most common cause is a point more than 50 m away from the road.

When the feature is saved, the Graphe routier panel opens again.

docs.title: Split a line at a point
docs.text:
This tool adds a button to the popup of the features of a line layer. It splits a line in two features at a point.

The button is only displayed if the user can modify the geometry and create features in this layer, in the Lizmap editing configuration. These rights can be changed with the constant ROAD_SPLIT_NEEDED_RIGHTS of the script (see Configure the script).

  1. Open the Graphe routier panel and click on the line where it must be split. A red point is displayed on the map.
  2. In the popup of the line, click the button. Its label is the title of the split_line_by_point action.
  3. Confirm the operation.

The script sends the red point to the action split_line_by_point. The database function road_graph.split_table_linestring_feature_by_point splits the line, and the layer is refreshed.

The two lines follow the direction of the road, even if the line was drawn in the opposite direction: the original feature keeps the first part, and the new feature gets the second part. Their start and end references are calculated in the direction of the road.

The default popup button of this action is hidden, because it does not send the clicked point.

docs.title: Merge two lines
docs.text:
This tool adds a button to the popup of the features of a line layer. It merges two features of the same layer into one feature.

The button is only displayed if the user can modify the geometry and create features in this layer, in the Lizmap editing configuration. The right to delete features is not required by default, even if the second feature is deleted. These rights can be changed with the constant ROAD_MERGE_NEEDED_RIGHTS of the script (see Configure the script).

  1. In the popup of the first line, click Choose this feature to merge. The button label becomes Feature chosen to merge. To cancel, click this button again.
  2. Click on the second line on the map. In its popup, click Merge with the chosen feature.
  3. Confirm the operation.

The script runs the action merge_selected_lines with the IDs of the two features. The database function road_graph.merge_table_linestring_features merges them and the layer is refreshed. The popup then shows only the merged feature.

The merged feature is the feature chosen first: it keeps its field values, and the second feature is deleted. Its references are calculated from the merged line, in the direction of the road.

Once a first feature is chosen, the merge button is only displayed for features of the same layer.

docs.title: 1. Publish the layers
docs.text:
In the QGIS project:

  • add the road_graph.edges layer. The actions about references use this layer.
  • add the road_graph.roads layer and publish it as WFS (Project properties > QGIS Server > WFS capabilities). The script uses it to fill the list of roads. The layer must have the fields id, road_code and road_order.
  • for the split and merge tools, add the line layers that the users can edit.

docs.title: 2. Create the database function
docs.text:
Create the function public.lizmap_get_data(json) in the database. The file lizmap_get_data_example.sql gives a complete example for all the actions.

The function uses the projection EPSG:2154. Change it if your data uses another projection.

docs.title: 3. Create the actions file
docs.text:
Create a file named after the QGIS project, with the extension .action. For example, for road_network.qgs, create road_network.qgs.action in the same folder.

The file lizmap_action_file_example.json gives a complete example. Update it:

  • replace edges_7df8a321_25e8_4a67_9bf8_796e4782e147 with the ID of your edges layer,
  • replace demo_painting_26eb3c57_3374_41a5_8628_391caa42f33a with the IDs of the line layers for the split and merge tools. Do this in layers and in callbacks.

The action names must not change, because the script uses them.

Action Scope Options Returned feature get_references_from_point layer road_code, vertex_number Point with road_code, marker_code, abscissa, cumulative, offset, side, vertex_number get_road_point_from_reference layer road_code, marker_code, abscissa, offset, side Point with the references get_road_substring_from_references layer road_code, start_marker_code, start_abscissa, end_marker_code, end_abscissa, offset, side Multilinestring with the start and end references get_edge_start_or_end_tip_from_references layer road_code, marker_code, abscissa, start_or_end (start or end), tip_type (edge or road) Point with marker_code, abscissa, start_or_end split_line_by_point feature none (the clicked point is sent as WKT) The clicked point, message and message_detail merge_selected_lines layer feature_id_a, feature_id_b message and message_detail, no geometry

vertex_number tells the script where to put the result: -1 for the panel, 0 for the start point and 1 for the end point of the edited geometry.

docs.title: 4. Configure the script
docs.text:
Open road_network.js and edit the CONFIGURATION section at the top of the file:

Constant Default value Description ROAD_MIN_SCALE 50000 Smallest scale denominator for the click and hover tools ROAD_ROADS_LAYER_NAME roads WFS name of the roads layer ROAD_EDGES_LAYER_ID edges_7df8a321_... QGIS ID of the edges layer ROAD_ORDER_FIELD road_order Field used to sort the list of roads ROAD_SPLIT_NEEDED_RIGHTS ['createFeature', 'modifyGeometry'] Editing rights needed on a line layer to display the split button ROAD_MERGE_NEEDED_RIGHTS ['createFeature', 'modifyGeometry'] Editing rights needed on a line layer to display the merge button. Add 'deleteFeature' to also require the right to delete features

The editing rights are the capabilities of the layer in the Lizmap editing configuration: createFeature (create features), modifyAttribute (modify the attributes), modifyGeometry (modify the geometry) and deleteFeature (delete features).

Do not edit the code below the END CONFIGURATION comment.

docs.title: 5. Add the files to Lizmap
docs.text:
Follow the Lizmap documentation: Adding your own JavaScript.

  1. Allow JavaScript for the repository in the Lizmap administration (Allow themes/JavaScript codes for this repository).
  2. Copy road_network.js, road_network.css and road_network.csv into the repository folder:
    • media/js/<project_name>/ to use the tools in one project,
    • media/js/default/ to use them in all projects of the repository.
  3. Reload the map in the browser.

docs.title: Translate the interface
docs.text:
The texts of the interface are written in English in the script. The translations are stored in a CSV file located next to the script. This file has the same name as the script, with the .csv extension: road_network.csv for road_network.js.

When the map loads, the script:

  1. gets the language of the user interface, from the lang attribute of the page or from the browser language,
  2. downloads the CSV file,
  3. displays the translated texts. A text without a translation is displayed in English.

If the CSV file is not found, the interface is displayed in English.

The first line of the file contains the language codes. The first column contains the English text, exactly as written in the script. Each other column contains the translations for one language:

en,fr
Road network,Graphe routier
Road,Route
"Please zoom in to at least 1:{scale} to display the references","Veuillez zoomer au moins au 1/{scale} pour afficher les références"

To add a language, add a column with its two-letter code, for example de or es.

Rules for the values:

  • enclose a value in double quotes if it contains a comma, a double quote or a new line,
  • double the double quotes inside a value: "",
  • keep the placeholders in braces, for example {scale}, and do not translate them. They are replaced by values when the text is displayed. They can be moved in the sentence.

docs.title: Texts of the actions and of the database
docs.text:
The same CSV file also translates:

  • the title and confirm properties of the actions, in the .qgs.action file. Write them in English, and add them to the CSV file.
  • the messages returned by the lizmap_get_data function, in the message field. Lizmap displays them at the top of the map, and the script replaces them by their translation.

A message can contain a variable part, for example the detail of an error returned by the database. In this case, the lizmap_get_data function must also return this variable part in a message_detail field, and the message must end with it:

Field Value message An error occurred while splitting the line: The point is not close enough to the feature (distance 12 > 5m) message_detail The point is not close enough to the feature (distance 12 > 5m)

In the CSV file, the variable part is replaced by the {detail} placeholder:

"An error occurred while splitting the line: {detail}","Une erreur s'est produite lors de la découpe de la ligne : {detail}"
