The variable part itself is not translated.

If you change a text in the .qgs.action file or in the lizmap_get_data function, change it in the CSV file too. Otherwise, the text is displayed without translation.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The script was written for a specific version of Lizmap Web Client. It may not work with another version.
  • The tools only support point and line layers.
  • The start and end references of a line must be on the same road.
  • The split and merge tools are not available for the edges layer.

docs.title: User guide
docs.text:
The RoadNetwork plugin stores all the business logic inside a PostgreSQL database. The QGIS plugin helps to create and upgrade this database, to visualize the road network, to edit it safely and to keep the business data up to date.

This guide is split in five parts:

  • Import data: how to import the road graph (edges and markers) into the database, and how to create a demo database.
  • QGIS project and tools: the administration project, the toolbar and panels of the plugin, and the tools available to search and get references.
  • Processing algorithms: the algorithms provided by the plugin.
  • Road graph editing: how to edit the roads, edges and markers in a dedicated editing session.
  • Check and fix the road graph: how to find and fix the issues of the road graph, for example after an import.
  • Managed objects: how to prepare the business data based on the road network, and how they are kept up to date when the graph changes.

docs.title: Database model
docs.text:
All the logic is stored inside a PostgreSQL database:

  • a simple set of tables: roads, edges, nodes, markers, glossary_road_class, managed_objects, and some views,
  • many functions to calculate references and geometries, among them:
    • get_road_point_from_reference
    • get_road_substring_from_references
    • update_table_references_from_geometries
    • update_table_geometry_from_references
  • trigger functions in charge of maintaining the road network topology: automatic node creation, split of intersected edges, etc.

See Tables and fields for the description of the fields of the tables, and the Database structure documentation for a complete description of the tables and functions.

docs.title: Administration tools
docs.text:
The plugin provides QGIS Processing algorithms which allow to:

  • create the database structure with all the tables, functions, etc.: Create database structure,
  • upgrade the structure automatically when upgrading the plugin: Upgrade database structure,
  • create a QGIS administration project with all the layers, styles, labels, actions, etc.: Create database local interface,
  • import data from template edges and markers tables: Import data from template.

These algorithms, described in Processing algorithms, are available in the QGIS Processing toolbox and in the RoadNetwork administration panel, which also shows the database connection used by the project and checks that the plugin and database versions match.

docs.title: Check and fix the road graph
docs.text:
After an import, the road graph often contains issues coming from the source data: crossing edges which are not cut, edges which should touch but do not, edges drawn in the opposite direction of the road, branches of a road using the code of the main road, etc.

The plugin provides tools to find these issues and, when possible, to fix them automatically.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
The issues must be fixed in an editing session, like any other modification of the road graph (see Road graph editing). Even after an import, use an editing session: draw a large editing session polygon if needed.

  1. Create an editing session covering the area to check.
  2. Run the algorithm Check the road graph on the schema of the editing session. The issues are stored in the table road_graph_editing.graph_issues, displayed by two layers added to the project: a point layer locating each issue, and a line layer showing the issues for which a line is useful.
  3. Review the issues, and fix them:
    • one by one with a right click on the issue (see Fix an issue with a right click),
    • or in batch: select the issues to fix automatically, then run the algorithm Fix the road graph issues with the option Selected features only. The issues already fixed are skipped,
    • or manually, for the issues without fix action (see the description of each check).
  4. After each fix, the roads of the issue are checked again: the fixed issue disappears, and the new issues of these roads appear. Refresh the map to see them. After manual changes, run the algorithm Check the road graph again: the same layers are updated.
  5. Merge the editing session: the table of the issues is emptied.

If the layers of the editing session are in editing mode, the fixes are run in their transaction: save the modifications of the layers afterwards, or cancel them. Else the fixes are saved at once.

The transaction is created by QGIS when the transaction mode of the project is Automatic transaction groups (Project properties, Data sources). If the layers are in editing mode without transaction, for example when the editing mode has been started before the transaction groups were created, the fixes are saved at once, unless the layers have modifications which are not saved yet: save or cancel them first. If needed, close and open again the project to create the transaction groups.

docs.title: Algorithms
docs.text:
The algorithm Check the road graph runs the checks on the schema of the editing session, for all the roads or only some of them, and updates the table of the issues: the issues found again keep their id. Only the issues inside the polygon of the editing session are kept. On the production schema, it creates two temporary layers, only to get an overview of the issues. The advanced parameter Options of the checks overrides the default options of the checks.

The algorithm Fix the road graph issues fixes the issues of one of these layers, in the order of their check codes, with their fix action. Check the option Selected features only to fix only the selected issues. The issues without fix action, and the issues already fixed, are skipped. The roads of the fixed issues are then checked again.

docs.title: Fix an issue with a right click
docs.text:
The layers of the issues have three actions. Use the Identify Features tool and right-click on an issue in the map, or use the Run Feature Action tool of the Attributes toolbar:

  • Fix this issue: fix the issue with its fix action. Nothing is done if the issue has no fix action,
  • Choose the fix of this issue…: choose the fix action among the actions of the check, then fix the issue. For example, for the check G01, cut the edges or mark them as not connected (bridge), and in this case choose the edge to mark,
  • Select the edges of this issue: select the edges of the issue in the edges layer of the editing session (road_graph_editing.edges) and zoom on them, for example to fix the issue manually.

In this example of the test data, the roads of an interchange cross the N814 on bridges without being connected, and an access road arrives on the roundabout without splitting it. This last issue has already been fixed: it is displayed in grey. A right click on a crossing of the N814 shows the actions:

The action Choose the fix of this issue… lists the fix actions of the check:

For the action mark_as_bridge, choose then the edge which must not be connected, or all the edges:

The result of the fix is stored in the fields fix_status (Fixed, Already fixed or Not fixed) and fix_message of the issue. The roads of the issue are then checked again: the fixed issue is deleted, and the issues which could not be fixed keep their error message. The layers of the editing session are refreshed.

The titles of the checks and of the actions, the labels of the fix actions and statuses and the messages are translated in the language of QGIS. The detailed messages returned by the database are in English.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
Each issue has:

  • a check code and title, and a severity: error or warning,
  • the road code, and the ids of the edges, nodes and markers concerned,
  • some details, for example a distance or an angle,
  • the fix action which can fix it automatically, and its parameters, or nothing if the issue must be fixed manually.

The checks are numbered in the recommended order of the fixes: the algorithm Fix the road graph issues fixes the issues in this order.

Each check below is illustrated by a diagram of the issue and of its fix.

Code Issue Fix G01 Edges crossing or touching each other without node cut_edges or mark_as_bridge G02 Edge ending near another edge without being connected (T junction) extend_edge G03 Nodes close to each other merge_nodes G04 Useless node: without edge, or between two edges of the same road delete_node G05 Edges in the opposite direction of the road reverse_edges G06 Previous and next edges inconsistent with the geometry relink_edges G07 Road with branches: more than two edges of the road at a node manual G08 Parallel edges of the same road, for example two carriageways manual G09 Short edge collapse_edge G10 First marker not at the start of the road move_marker G11 Markers not in the order of the road manual G12 Duplicate edges, for example after a copy of an edge delete_duplicate_edges

To fix an issue with another action than the proposed one, or to choose the action of an issue without action, use the action Choose the fix of this issue…. Before running the algorithm Fix the road graph issues, you can also change the field fix_action (and fix_params if needed) of the issues layer, and save it.

docs.title: G01: Crossing edges without node
docs.text:
Two edges crossing or touching each other must be split by a node, unless they are not connected, for example on a bridge or in a tunnel: the edges with the field no_intersection_cutting set to True are ignored (see Edges which must not be cut).

The check returns one issue for each point where two edges cross or touch each other, if this point is not the start or end point of both edges (50 cm tolerance, like the triggers splitting the edges). The field details gives:

  • crossing_type:
    • touching: the point is the start or end point of one of the edges, for example a road arriving on another road without splitting it. The edges are surely connected: the fix action is cut_edges,
    • crossing: the edges cross each other. They may be on a bridge: the fix action must be chosen for each issue,
  • road_codes and road_classes: the codes and classes of the roads of the two edges, for example a highway crossing a departmental road is probably a bridge,
  • angle: the angle between the two edges, from 0 (parallel) to 90 degrees (perpendicular).

Fix actions:

  • cut_edges: create a node at the point, or use the existing node less than 50 cm from it, which splits the edges passing there,
  • mark_as_bridge: set the field no_intersection_cutting to True for the two edges, or only for the edge given by the key edge_id added to fix_params, for example {"point": "SRID=2154;POINT(455144.6 6905485.8)", "edge_ids": [2839, 2841], "edge_id": 2839}.

If most of the crossings are bridges, or are crossroads, set the option crossing_fix_action of the check to mark_as_bridge or cut_edges: the issues of type crossing then get this fix action. Check the result carefully afterwards.

UPDATE road_graph.glossary_graph_check
SET default_options = default_options || '{"crossing_fix_action": "mark_as_bridge"}'
WHERE code = 'G01';

docs.title: G02: Edge ending near another edge
docs.text:
A road arriving on another road must be connected to it. In the source data, it often stops a few decimeters before the other road, or a little beyond it.

The check returns one issue for each free end of an edge, i.e. an end with no other edge connected to it, located less than the tolerance from another edge: option tolerance, 2 m by default. Are ignored:

  • the edges connected to the opposite end of the edge, for example its next edge if it is very short,
  • the edges crossed by the edge near its free end: the edge goes a little beyond the other edge. The crossing is found by the check G01.

When two free ends are close to each other, only one issue is returned.

The point to join is the closest point of the other edge, or its start or end point if it is less than 50 cm from it. The field details gives the road codes of the two edges, the distance, and the join_type: edge (middle of the other edge) or edge_end.

Fix action:

  • extend_edge: connect the free end of the edge to the point to join:
    • if the point to join is the start or end point of the other edge, the free end is connected to its node, and the node of the free end is deleted,
    • else, if the free end is less than 50 cm from the other edge, the node of the free end is moved to the point to join,
    • else, the point to join is added at the free end of the edge, and the node of the free end follows.

In the two last cases, the triggers split the other edge there. Like any geometry of the road graph, the coordinates are rounded to 10 cm.

-- Find the gaps up to 3 m
UPDATE road_graph.glossary_graph_check
SET default_options = default_options || '{"tolerance": 3}'
WHERE code = 'G02';

docs.title: G03: Nodes close to each other
docs.text:
Two nodes a few centimeters or decimeters from each other should usually be the same node: the roads arriving there are not connected in the graph.

The check returns one issue for each pair of nodes less than the tolerance from each other: option tolerance, 1 m by default. The nodes linked by an edge are ignored: this edge is very short, and must be examined with the check of the short edges.

The node to keep is the node with the most edges, so that the fewest edges are moved, or else the node with the lowest id, i.e. the oldest node. It is the first node of node_ids, and the point of the issue. The field details gives the road codes of the edges of the two nodes and the distance.

Many of these issues are also found by the check G02, when an edge ends near the start or end point of another edge: they are skipped once fixed by G02.

Fix action:

  • merge_nodes: move the start and end points of the edges of the other node to the node to keep, then delete the other node.

docs.title: G04: Useless node
docs.text:
A node is useful at a junction, or at the start or end of a road. The source data often contains other nodes, for example where the source features of a road were split: these nodes split the road into several edges for nothing.

The check returns one issue, with the severity warning, for each node:

  • without edge (node_type: no_edge), only when all the roads are checked,
  • or between two edges of the same road (node_type: two_edges): one edge arrives at the node, and the other one leaves it. Are ignored the edges with different values of no_intersection_cutting, the two edges forming a loop, and the edges crossing each other, for example a loop ramp of an interchange.

Two edges of the same road arriving both at the node, or leaving it both, are in opposite directions: this issue is found by the check of the reversed edges.

Fix action:

  • delete_node: delete the node. The triggers merge the two edges into the edge with the lowest id, which keeps its other fields, for example id_source.

Fix the issues of the checks G01 and G03 before: else the triggers would split the merged edge at its crossings with the other edges, which may be bridges, or connect it to the close nodes. In this case, the fix returns an error and nothing is changed.

docs.title: G05: Edges in the opposite direction of the road
docs.text:
The edges of a road must be drawn in the direction of the road, from its first marker to its last one: the references (marker and abscissa) and the order of the edges depend on it.

The check groups the edges of each road in sequences: two edges follow each other at a node where there are only these two edges of the road. The direction of a sequence is given:

  • by the order of the markers of the road located along it (reason: markers), less than the option marker_tolerance from it, 10 m by default,
  • or else, without enough markers, by the direction of most of the length of its edges (reason: neighbours).

The markers of the roundabouts are not used, and the roundabouts, whose edges form a ring, are not checked. The direction of an edge is given by its geometry, not by its fields start_node and end_node.

The check returns one issue for each group of consecutive edges in the opposite direction of their sequence. A whole road drawn in the opposite direction of its markers is also found. The field details gives the reason, the number of edges and their length, and the number of consecutive markers in the direction of the road (markers_in_road_direction) and in the opposite direction.

Fix action:

  • reverse_edges: reverse the geometry of the edges. The triggers swap their start and end nodes, and calculate again their previous and next edges and the references of the road.

A geometry can also be reversed manually, for example with the QGIS tool Reverse Line.

-- Use the markers up to 20 m from the edges
UPDATE road_graph.glossary_graph_check
SET default_options = default_options || '{"marker_tolerance": 20}'
WHERE code = 'G05';

docs.title: G06: Previous and next edges inconsistent with the geometry
docs.text:
The fields previous_edge_id and next_edge_id of the edges give the order of the edges of the road, used to calculate the references. They are set by the triggers, but can be wrong after an import, or after modifications made without the triggers. The references of the whole road are then wrong.

The check returns one issue for each road with edges whose next edge:

  • does not start at the end node of the edge, whereas another edge of the road starts there,
  • or is connected to another edge, or to the edge in the opposite direction.

The previous edge is checked the same way. The roundabouts are ignored.

When the road is interrupted, for example by a roundabout, the last edge before the gap and the first edge after it do not touch each other: only their link gives the order of the road. The last edge before the gap is linked to:

  • for a wrong link, the first edge of the piece of road of the linked edge,
  • for a missing link, the closest piece of road starting less than the option gap_tolerance (150 m by default) from the end of the edge, if this piece is not before the edge in the order of the road.

The other links across a gap are kept. The field details gives the number of edges and, for each edge, its previous and next edges (previous_edge_id, next_edge_id) and the expected ones (expected_previous_edge_id, expected_next_edge_id).

Fix action:

  • relink_edges: set the expected previous and next edges of the road: the edges connected by the nodes, the edges on the other side of a gap, or no link. Then the references of the road are calculated again.

Fix the issues of the checks G03 and G05 before: two close nodes or a reversed edge break the links. The next checks use the order of the edges.

docs.title: G07: Road with branches
docs.text:
A road must be a line: its edges follow each other, without branches. The ramps of an interchange or of a roundabout, or the two carriageways of a road, must have their own road code. Else the order of the edges of the road, and so the references, cannot be calculated.

The check returns one issue for each node with more than two edges of the same road. The roundabouts are ignored. The main line of the road at the node is given by the edge arriving at the node and the edge leaving it which are the most aligned: the other edges are the branches. The field details gives the number of edges at the node (edge_count), and the ids of the edges of the main line (main_edge_ids) and of the branches (branch_edge_ids). The line of the issue shows the branches.

There is no fix action: give another road code to the edges of the branches, for example a new road for a ramp. Check the main line proposed by the check, especially when the edges are not in the direction of the road (check G05).

docs.title: G08: Parallel edges of the same road
docs.text:
The two carriageways of a road must have their own road code. When they use the same code without being connected, the check G07 does not find them.

The check returns one issue, with the severity warning, for each pair of edges of the same road, not connected by a node, which run along each other:

  • less than the option tolerance from each other, 30 m by default,
  • along at least the option min_length, 10 m by default.

The edges which only approach each other are ignored, for example the edges of a road on both sides of a roundabout: each edge must run along the other one on at least the minimum length. The roundabouts are ignored. The field details gives the distance between the edges and the length along which they are parallel (parallel_length). The line of the issue shows the parallel parts of the edges.

There is no fix action: give another road code to one of the carriageways. A road which comes back near itself, for example a hairpin bend, can also be found: in this case, there is nothing to fix.

docs.title: G09: Short edge
docs.text:
A very short edge often comes from the digitizing: for example two junctions a few decimeters from each other instead of a crossroads, or a small piece of road left at the end of an edge.

The check returns one issue for each edge shorter than the option min_length, 3 m by default. The edges of the roundabouts, and the edges arriving at a roundabout or leaving it, are often short: they are ignored, unless they are reduced to a point (less than 10 cm, the precision of the coordinates). The severity is error for an edge reduced to a point, else warning. The field details gives the length, the number of other edges at the start and end nodes (start_edge_count and end_edge_count), and is_roundabout_edge.

Fix action:

  • collapse_edge: delete the edge and merge its two nodes into the node to keep: the node with the most edges, or else the node with the lowest id, which is the first node of node_ids. At the other node, the next or previous edge of the same road is extended with the geometry of the short edge up to the node to keep: the geometry and the length of the road are kept. The start and end points of the edges of the other roads are moved to the node to keep: their last segment is redirected, by less than the length of the short edge.

The only edge of a road has no fix action: the road would not have any edge anymore.

docs.title: G10: First marker not at the start of the road
docs.text:
The first marker of a road is the marker with the lowest code and abscissa: it is often the marker 0, but it can be a virtual marker with a higher code. It must be at the start point of the first edge of the road, the edge without previous edge. When it is a few centimeters after it, the start of the road has no reference.

The check returns one issue for each road whose first marker is more than 5 cm from the start of the road. The roundabouts are ignored. The severity is error if the start of the first edge has no reference, else warning. The field details gives the marker_code, marker_abscissa and is_virtual of the marker, its distance to the start of the road, its position along the first edge (position_on_edge), and has_start_reference.

Fix action:

  • move_marker: move the marker to the start of the road. The references of the road are calculated again. It is only proposed when the marker is less than the option tolerance from the start of the road, 1 m by default. Farther, check the road manually: the marker may be right, and the first edge wrong, for example when the road is in the opposite direction (check G05).

docs.title: G11: Markers not in the order of the road
docs.text:
Sorted by code and abscissa, the markers of a road must follow each other along the road: else, the references calculated from them are wrong.

The position of each marker along its road is the cumulative length of the road at its closest edge, less than the option marker_tolerance from it, 50 m by default. The check keeps the longest sequence of markers in the order of the road, two markers being allowed at the same position (1 m tolerance), for example a virtual marker and the marker of the next code with the same reference. It returns one issue for each other marker (issue_type: order), and for each marker far from its road (far_from_road) or whose closest edge has no reference (edge_without_reference). The roundabouts are ignored.

The field details gives the code, abscissa, type and position of the marker, and the code and position of the previous and next markers in the order of the road.

There is no fix action: move the marker, or change its code. Fix the issues of the check G05 before: a reversed edge changes the positions of the markers.

docs.title: G12: Duplicate edges
docs.text:
Two edges are duplicates when they have the same end nodes, in the same or the opposite direction, and the same geometry: their Hausdorff distance is less than the option tolerance, 0.5 m by default. It happens for example after a copy of an edge. The duplicates also create issues G07, and often G06: although this check is numbered last, fix its issues first.

The check returns one issue for each edge with duplicates: the kept edge is the edge with the lowest id. The field details gives the kept_edge_id, the duplicate_edge_ids, their road_codes and the length.

Fix action:

  • delete_duplicate_edges: delete the duplicates, one by one: the previous and next edges of each deleted edge are linked together. It is only proposed when all the edges have the same road. The duplicates of another road, for example a common section of two roads drawn twice, must be checked manually.

docs.title: Configuration of the checks
docs.text:
The checks are listed in the table road_graph.glossary_graph_check, with for each check: its code, title, severity, function, fix actions and description. The rows are added by the plugin migrations. The administrator can modify two columns:

  • default_options: the default options of the check, for example its tolerance in meters,
  • is_active: uncheck it to stop running the check by default. It is still run if it is explicitly asked.
-- Give the action mark_as_bridge to the edges crossing each other found by the check G01
UPDATE road_graph.glossary_graph_check
SET default_options = default_options || '{"crossing_fix_action": "mark_as_bridge"}'
WHERE code = 'G01';

The checks are always read from the production schema, even when the editing session is checked.

docs.title: Database functions
docs.text:
The algorithms use the following database functions, which can also be used directly in SQL. They are installed in the production schema road_graph and in the editing schema road_graph_editing.

  • road_graph.check_graph(_checks, _road_codes, _options): run the checks and return one line per issue. All the active checks are run if _checks is NULL, and all the roads are checked if _road_codes is NULL. The parameter _options overrides the default options of the checks, with the check code as key.
-- Check all the roads of the editing session
SELECT * FROM road_graph_editing.check_graph();

-- Check only some roads, with some checks and an option
SELECT *
FROM road_graph_editing.check_graph(
    ARRAY['G01'],
    ARRAY['D40', 'D16'],
    '{"G01": {"crossing_fix_action": "cut_edges"}}'
);
  • road_graph_editing.fix_graph_issue(_fix_action, _params): fix an issue with its fix action and parameters. It only works in the editing schema. It returns a JSON object with the keys status (success, skipped if the issue has already been fixed, or error) and message.
SELECT road_graph_editing.fix_graph_issue(i.fix_action, i.fix_params)
FROM road_graph_editing.check_graph(ARRAY['G01']) AS i
WHERE i.fix_action IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY i.id;

docs.title: Editing rules
docs.text:
The road graph data are not edited directly in the production schema road_graph, but in a dedicated editing session schema road_graph_editing, which acts as a sandbox. The editing is made in four steps, described below.

At any time, the modifications of the editing session can be highlighted with the action Display edited data, and the editing session can be cancelled with the action Drop editing session.

docs.title: Draw the editing session polygon
docs.text: The user draws a polygon in the editing_sessions layer around the area to edit. The new editing session has the status created.

docs.title: Clone the data into the sandbox
docs.text: The algorithm Clone data to a new editing session (toolbar button Clone data to the editing sandbox, or layer action Create editing session) copies an extract of the production data inside this polygon into the sandbox. The status becomes cloned.

docs.title: Edit the data
docs.text:
The editing is made with the QGIS tools: forms, topological editing, etc. The status becomes edited after the first change.

  • QGIS automatic transaction grouping is activated in the project: the changes made by the database triggers (node creation, edge split, etc.) are visible live.
  • A layer action helps to create roundabouts, see Create a roundabout.

docs.title: Merge the editing session
docs.text: The algorithm Merge editing session data (toolbar button Merge editing sandbox data) merges the modifications back into the road_graph schema and updates the managed objects. The sandbox data and the merged editing session are then deleted.

docs.title: Do not edit the production schema directly
docs.text:
Do not edit the production schema road_graph directly

The layers of the production schema road_graph can technically be edited, but some automatic processes only work with an editing session:

  • the intersections between edges are only cut inside the editing session polygon. Without an editing session, a new edge crossing a road is not connected to it, without any error message, and the road graph becomes wrong,
  • the managed objects (business data) are only updated when an editing session is merged: their references or geometries are no longer right after a direct modification of the road graph,
  • the modifications are not logged: they cannot be displayed with the action Display edited data, nor cancelled with the action Drop editing session,
  • the modifications are immediately visible by all the users, for example in Lizmap.

Always edit the road graph in an editing session.

Correct the whole road graph after a first import

The editing session polygon can cover all the data, for example a rectangle around the whole road graph, to correct the data after a first import. The performance is the same as with a small editing session: with the demo data (7,809 edges), the data are cloned in about 1 second, and the edits and the merge take the same time. But only one editing session can be edited at a time: the other users must wait for the merge to edit the road graph.

docs.title: Editing session actions
docs.text: The editing_sessions layer has three layer actions. To run an action on an editing session, use the Identify Features tool and right-click on the editing session polygon in the map, or use the Run Feature Action tool of the Attributes toolbar. See also Layer actions.

docs.title: Create editing session
docs.text: This action opens the algorithm Clone data to a new editing session, which copies the production data inside the last created editing session polygon into the editing schema, like the toolbar button Clone data to the editing sandbox. It is a layer action: it is available in the Actions menu of the editing_sessions attribute table toolbar, and does not need any selected feature.

docs.title: Display edited data
docs.text:
This action highlights in the map the objects modified in the editing session, from the content of its logged_ids column of the layer editing_sessions. The objects flash with a color depending on the modification:

Color Modification Layer used to display the object Yellow Updated the editing layer, e.g. edges copie Red Deleted the production layer, e.g. edges Green Inserted the editing layer, e.g. edges copie

The edges, nodes and markers are displayed. A message is displayed if the editing session does not contain any modification.

docs.title: Drop editing session
docs.text:
This action deletes the editing session and all the data of the editing schema road_graph_editing, with the database function road_graph.drop_editing_session. The modifications which have not been merged are lost: a confirmation is asked before.

The action is cancelled with a warning if:

  • the editing_sessions layer is not in editing mode,
  • the tool Get references on hover is activated: uncheck the checkbox Get references on hover ? in the Road network tools panel before.

You may have to refresh the map canvas to see the changes.

Info

Do not forget to save the state by clicking on the Save button of QGIS editing toolbar.

docs.title: Create a roundabout
docs.text:
Roundabouts have their own road code, e.g. GIR_D40_D80, and cut the other roads (see Concepts). The road of the roundabout must exist in the roads layer with the road type roundabout.

To create a roundabout in the editing session:

  1. Toggle editing on the edges layer.
  2. Use the QGIS shape digitizing tool Circle by a center point and another point to draw the roundabout circle, and give it the road code of the roundabout.
  3. Once the circle is created, the database trigger functions automatically split the circle into edges at each intersection with the edges of the existing crossroads.
  4. Right-click on one of the edges of the roundabout circle with the Identify Features tool, and choose the action Finalize the roundabout.

This layer action of the edges copie layer runs the database function clean_digitized_roundabout, which:

  • deletes the pieces of edges inside the roundabout, and updates the previous and next edges of the remaining roads. The edges marked as not to be cut at the intersections (no_intersection_cutting) are kept: they are at another level, for example a road passing under the roundabout,
  • deletes the node created by QGIS at the top of the circle, by merging the two edges around it,
  • adds a marker 0 for this roundabout, on its westernmost node, if it does not already exist.

The action is cancelled with a warning if the layer is not in editing mode, or if the road type of the selected edge is not roundabout. It fails with an error if the circle is not connected to any road: the edges crossing it must not be marked as not connected (see Edges which must not be cut), otherwise they are not cut by the circle. Uncheck their field no_intersection_cutting and draw the circle again. You may have to refresh the map canvas to see the changes.

docs.title: Edges which must not be cut
docs.text:
By default, the database trigger functions keep the graph topology up to date while you edit:

  • when an edge is drawn or its geometry is modified, a node is created at each intersection of this edge with the other edges, and the crossing edges are split by this node. If a node already exists less than 50 cm from the intersection, it is used instead.
  • when a node is created or moved on an edge, far enough from its start and end points, this edge is split by the node. This is also the case of the start or end node of an edge being drawn, for example a new road arriving in the middle of another road.

Only the intersections of the drawn or modified edge are processed, and only inside the editing session polygon. The intersections between the other edges are kept as they are: two edges crossing each other without a node, for example at an existing bridge, stay without a node, even when one of them is split by the drawn edge.

But two roads drawn on top of each other are not always connected: a highway crossing a road on a bridge, a road going through a tunnel, the access roads of a highway interchange, etc. For these edges, check the field No intersection cutting (no_intersection_cutting) in the edge form. It can be changed at any time, for example before drawing or modifying a road which crosses a bridge.

An edge with no_intersection_cutting set to True:

  • is not split at its intersections with the other edges, and does not split them: no node is created at these intersections, whether the field is set on the drawn edge or on the crossed edge,
  • is not split by the existing nodes located under it, for example a crossroad of the roads located under a bridge, even when such a node is moved,
  • is split when the start or end point of a drawn or moved edge is located on it, far enough from its own start and end points: for example a new access road arriving in the middle of a highway edge. This makes sense since the two roads are really connected at this point.

The value of the field is kept when an edge is split: the new parts have the same value.

The diagram below shows when an edge is split:

graph TD A[A node is created or moved on an edge,<br>or a drawn or modified edge crosses it] --> B{Field No intersection cutting<br>of this edge, or of the drawn edge} B -->|False| C[The edge is split] B -->|True| D{Is the node the start or end point<br>of the edge being drawn or moved?} D -->|Yes, e.g. a new access road<br>arriving on a highway| C D -->|No, e.g. a road crossing<br>under a bridge| E[The edge is not split]

Tip

Before drawing a new road which crosses a highway interchange without being connected to it, set the field to True for the new edge, or for the crossed highway and access roads edges: no node will be created at these intersections, and only the roads really connected will be split.

docs.title: Impacts of the modifications on the references
docs.text:
The references of each edge, at its start and end points, are calculated automatically by the database trigger functions (see Tables and fields):

  • the marker and the abscissa: the last marker before the point, and the distance from this marker,
  • the cumulative distance: the distance from the start of the road.

They only depend on what is located before the point, in the direction of the road. A modification of the road graph therefore only impacts the references downstream of it:

  1. The geometry of an edge is modified, for example when a vertex is moved: the road becomes longer or shorter.
    • the references of the edges upstream of the modified edge do not change,
    • the markers and abscissas change from the modified edge up to the next marker, real or virtual. After it, the abscissas are measured from this marker, which has not moved,
    • the cumulative distances change for all the edges downstream, up to the end of the road.
  2. An edge is split by a node, for example at a new crossroad: the geometry of the road does not change. Only the two parts of the split edge get their new references: the references of all the other edges do not change. This is the fastest modification, even on a long road.
  3. A marker is moved, added or deleted: the markers and abscissas change between the old or new position of the marker and the next marker. The cumulative distances do not change.

When the editing session is merged, the managed objects of the modified roads are updated with the same logic: for example, an object located downstream of a lengthened edge gets a greater cumulative distance, and a greater abscissa if it is located before the next marker. See Example: impacts of a graph modification.

Note

After a modification of the geometry of a road or of its markers, the references are only calculated again for the edges downstream of the modification: a modification near the end of a long road is faster than a modification near its start. For example, on a road of 118 km with 135 edges, moving a vertex takes about 1.5 s near the start of the road, and 0.3 s near its end.

docs.title: How to edit the data in QGIS
docs.text:
In QGIS, you can edit the layer data by toggling the editing mode for each layer:

  • Select the layer in the panel by clicking on it: the layer is highlighted in blue
  • Right-click on the layer name and select Toggle Editing or use the menu Layer / Toggle Editing

To add a new record, select the layer in the Layers panel, then use the menu Edit / Add Record (or CTRL+.). It will open a form which lets you enter the needed data. Once every required fields have been filled, validate with the OK button on the bottom-right.

To view all the records of a layer, select the layer in the Layers panel, then open the attribute table with the menu Layer / Open Attribute Table (or F6)

You can undo previous modifications with the menu Edit / Undo (or CTRL+Z).

To permanently save the changed data in the layer, you need to use the menu Layer / Save Layer Edits. After saving the data, you will not be able to undo your changes (but you can always reopen the data and changed the values).

To edit a record, open the layer attribute table, and then click on the small button Switch to form view on the bottom-right of the dialog (the first one). Then select a record in the left panel, and use the displayed form to edit the data.

To delete a record, select the record in the attribute table by clicking on the line number on the left: the line must be highlighted in blue. Then use the trash icon Delete selected features (or Del). You can undo the deletion if you have not yet saved layer edits.

docs.title: Import the road graph: edges and markers
docs.text:
The road graph tables roads, edges, nodes and markers can be filled from two vector layers: one for the edges and one for the markers.

These layers must follow the structure of the template files provided with the plugin, in the folder roadnetwork/resources/import/ of the plugin:

  • source_edges.fgb for the edges,
  • source_markers.fgb for the markers.

You can open these FlatGeobuf files in QGIS to see example data.

docs.title: Edges layer
docs.text:
Each feature is an edge, i.e. a portion of a road between two nodes, drawn in the direction of the road.

  • Geometry: LineString, or MultiLineString with only one part (only the first part of a multi-part geometry is imported).
  • Columns:
Column Type Description road_code text Code of the road, e.g. D248. The roads are created from the distinct values. edge_order integer Order of the edge in its road, from the start of the road: 1, 2, 3, etc. road_type text road or roundabout road_class text Class of the road. It must exist in the table glossary_road_class, e.g. Départementale road_class_code text Code of the road class, e.g. the code of the French department is_active boolean If the road is active road_topic text Optional topic of the road, e.g. Port. Can be empty. is_access_road boolean If the road is an access road id_source text Identifier of the feature in the source data. Can be empty.

The previous and next edges of each edge are calculated from the edge_order column.

docs.title: Markers layer
docs.text:
Each feature is a marker (reference point, PR) positioned along a road.

  • Geometry: Point, or MultiPoint with only one point.
  • Columns:
Column Type Description road_code text Code of the road of the marker. It must correspond to a road_code of the edges layer. code integer Code of the marker, e.g. 12 for PR 12. Must be positive. abscissa real Abscissa of the marker, in meters. Must be positive. Use 0 for the real markers. is_virtual boolean True for a virtual marker, False for a real marker. id_source text Identifier of the feature in the source data. Can be empty.

A marker 0 with an abscissa 0 is automatically created at the start of each road, if it does not already exist.

docs.title: Run the import
docs.text:
Use the Processing algorithm Import data from template, also available with the button Import data of the RoadNetwork administration panel:

  • PostgreSQL connection to the database: the database where the plugin structure has been installed,
  • Edges: the edges layer,
  • Markers: the markers layer.

The algorithm:

  1. checks that the layers contain the required columns,
  2. copies the layers in temporary tables, reprojected to the coordinate reference system of the database,
  3. runs the database function road_graph.import_data_from_template_tables, which:
    • checks the values of road_type and road_class,
    • creates the roads, the nodes at the start and end of each edge, the edges and the markers,
    • calculates the references of the edges (start and end markers, abscissas and cumulative distances),
  4. displays the number of imported roads, edges, nodes and markers, and drops the temporary tables.

Note

This import is designed to initialize an empty road graph. Existing objects are not updated: conflicting data are ignored.

docs.title: Create a demo database
docs.text:
The template files provided with the plugin contain a complete demo road graph, in Normandy (France), in the coordinate reference system EPSG:2154 - RGF93 v1 / Lambert-93:

  • 2,260 roads: departmental and national roads, highways, roundabouts, etc.,
  • 7,809 edges,
  • 13,774 markers.

It is useful to train the users or to test the features of the plugin without modifying the production data.

Since the plugin schema is always road_graph, a database contains only one road graph: use a dedicated PostgreSQL database for the demo, for example road_network_demo, with the PostGIS extension.

  1. In QGIS, add a connection to this database, and configure the plugin with it.
  2. Run the algorithm Create database structure, with the default coordinate reference system EPSG:2154.
  3. Open the template files source_edges.fgb and source_markers.fgb in QGIS. They are stored in the plugin folder: use the menu Settings / User Profiles / Open Active Profile Folder, then open the folder python/plugins/roadnetwork/resources/import/.
  4. Run the algorithm Import data from template with these two layers, as described above.
  5. Run the algorithm Create database local interface to create the QGIS administration project of the demo database, and open it.

To add some demo business data, follow the examples of the page Managed objects.

docs.title: Business data
docs.text: To import your business data (road signs, safety barriers, etc.) and calculate their references, see Managed objects: add a business table.

docs.title: Managed objects
docs.text:
The local authorities manage a lot of data based on the road network: roadworks, asphalt rehabilitation, road signs, hedge pruning, etc.

Each data object, point or (multi)linestring, is defined by its references calculated from the road network (see Concepts). They are stored in your own PostgreSQL tables, called managed objects. When the road graph is modified, these objects must be updated.

docs.title: The managed objects layer
docs.text:
The managed_objects layer lists all the PostgreSQL tables impacted by any graph modification, with the update policy to apply to each of them:

id schema_name table_name geometry_type update_policy_on_graph_change add_trigger_on_geom_change 1 managed demo_trees POINT references True 2 managed demo_safety_barriers MULTILINESTRING geometry False
  • schema_name and table_name: the business table,
  • geometry_type: the geometry type of the table, e.g. POINT or MULTILINESTRING,
  • update_policy_on_graph_change: the rule chosen by the administrator:
    • references: the geometry is kept and the references are updated,
    • geometry: the references are kept and the geometry is updated.
  • add_trigger_on_geom_change: if True, the trigger calculating the references, and for the line tables the trigger updating the connected lines, are created on this table by the function road_graph.add_managed_objects_triggers() (see below). Default: False.

Each table must have the reference columns corresponding to its geometry type. They can be added automatically with the function road_graph.add_managed_object_reference_fields, for one table or for all the tables of this layer (see Add the reference fields).

docs.title: Add a business table
docs.text:
To manage a new business table with the road graph:

  1. prepare the table, with its reference columns,
  2. register it in the managed_objects layer,
  3. add the reference columns if needed,
  4. calculate the references of its features,
  5. optionally, calculate automatically the references of the features created or moved afterwards.

docs.title: Prepare the table
docs.text:
The table must have:

  • a primary key,
  • a geometry column geom, in the same coordinate reference system as the road graph, of type Point for point objects, or LineString / MultiLineString for linear objects,
  • a text column road_code,
  • the reference columns, which are calculated from the road graph:
Geometry type Required columns Optional columns Point marker_code (integer), abscissa (real) cumulative (real), offset (real), side (text) (Multi)LineString start_marker_code (integer), start_abscissa (real), end_marker_code (integer), end_abscissa (real) start_cumulative, end_cumulative (real), offset (real), side (text)

For example, for a table of trees:

CREATE TABLE managed.demo_trees (
    id integer PRIMARY KEY GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY,
    species text NOT NULL,
    road_code text,
    marker_code integer,
    abscissa real,
    side text,
    "offset" real,
    cumulative real,
    geom geometry(POINT, 2154)
);

The reference columns can also be added automatically, once the table is created, with the function road_graph.add_managed_object_reference_fields (see Add the reference fields).

Then import your data into this table, for example with the QGIS tools (drag and drop in the Browser panel, or the Processing algorithm Export to PostgreSQL), or with SQL.

docs.title: Register the table
docs.text:
Add the table in the managed_objects layer (table road_graph.managed_objects), with its schema name, table name, geometry type and update policy:

INSERT INTO road_graph.managed_objects (
    schema_name, table_name, geometry_type, update_policy_on_graph_change
)
VALUES ('managed', 'demo_trees', 'POINT', 'references');

docs.title: Add the reference fields
docs.text:
The function road_graph.add_managed_object_reference_fields adds to a table the reference columns listed above, depending on its geometry type. The geometry type is read from the managed_objects layer if the table is registered, or else from its geometry column geom.

For example, for a table of road signs which does not have the reference columns yet:

CREATE TABLE managed.road_signs (
    id integer PRIMARY KEY GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY,
    label text,
    geom geometry(POINT, 2154)
);

-- Add the reference fields
SELECT * FROM road_graph.add_managed_object_reference_fields('managed', 'road_signs');

The function returns one line per column, with its status:

field_name field_type field_status road_code text added marker_code integer added abscissa real added cumulative real added offset real added side text added
  • The existing columns are not modified: their status is already exists, or already exists with the type ... if their type is not the expected one. The function can therefore be run several times.
  • The optional columns (cumulative, start_cumulative, end_cumulative, offset and side) are not added if the third parameter is False: road_graph.add_managed_object_reference_fields('managed', 'road_signs', False).
  • If the columns cannot be added, the function returns one line with the status table not found, geom column not found or geometry type not supported: ....

To add the reference columns to all the tables listed in the managed_objects layer:

SELECT o.schema_name, o.table_name, f.field_name, f.field_type, f.field_status
FROM road_graph.managed_objects AS o
CROSS JOIN LATERAL road_graph.add_managed_object_reference_fields(o.schema_name, o.table_name) AS f
ORDER BY o.id;

Tip

The column road_code is added empty. If it is still empty when the references are calculated, the references are calculated on the closest road, and the column road_code is filled. Fill it beforehand to force the road of a feature, for example at an intersection.

docs.title: Calculate the references
docs.text:
Once the features have been imported, calculate their references from their geometries with the database function road_graph.update_table_references_from_geometries:

-- Calculate the references of all the features of the table
SELECT road_graph.update_table_references_from_geometries('managed', 'demo_trees', NULL);

-- Calculate the references of the features of some roads only
SELECT road_graph.update_table_references_from_geometries('managed', 'demo_trees', ARRAY['D138', 'D152']);

The function parameters are the schema name, the table name, and an optional list of road codes. For each feature:

  • if the column road_code is filled, the references are calculated on this road,
  • if it is empty, the closest road is used, and the column road_code is filled.

It returns the number of updated features and their ids, for example:

{"nb": 7, "last_updated_objects_ids": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]}

If your data contain the references but no geometry, use instead the function road_graph.update_table_geometries_from_references, with the same parameters, to calculate the geometries from the references.

docs.title: Automatic calculation of the references
docs.text:
The trigger function road_graph.calculate_managed_object_references calculates the references of a managed object feature each time it is inserted or its geometry is updated. The table must be listed in road_graph.managed_objects, and have a road_code and a geom column.

The function road_graph.add_managed_objects_triggers() creates this trigger, named trg_calculate_managed_object_references, on every table listed in road_graph.managed_objects with the column add_trigger_on_geom_change set to True. For the linestring and multilinestring tables, it also creates the trigger trg_update_managed_object_linked_geometries (see Automatic update of the connected lines). Run it after adding new tables in the managed objects layer, or after checking this column:

SELECT * FROM road_graph.add_managed_objects_triggers();

It can be run several times: each trigger is only created when it does not already exist. Unchecking add_trigger_on_geom_change does not remove an existing trigger. The function returns one line per trigger, with its status, or one line without trigger name when no trigger can be created for the table:

schema_name table_name trigger_name trigger_status public demo_painting trg_calculate_managed_object_references created public demo_painting trg_update_managed_object_linked_geometries created public demo_trees trg_calculate_managed_object_references already exists public demo_nogeom geom column not found public missing_table table not found public demo_signs not requested

For each table, the created trigger is equivalent to:

CREATE TRIGGER trg_calculate_managed_object_references
BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF geom
ON public.demo_painting
FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE PROCEDURE road_graph.calculate_managed_object_references();

docs.title: Automatic update of the connected lines
docs.text:
The trigger function road_graph.update_managed_object_linked_geometries keeps the lines connected when the geometry of a line is updated: the other lines of the same table and the same road whose start or end point touched (5 cm tolerance) the start or end point of the line before its modification are shortened or extended to stay connected to it:

  • an upstream line gets the new start references of the line as end references,
  • a downstream line gets the new end references of the line as start references.

Their geometry is calculated again from their references with the function road_graph.get_road_substring_from_references, keeping their offset and side. The cumulative distances are also updated if the table has the fields start_cumulative and end_cumulative. A connected line is not modified if the updated line now covers it entirely.

The table must be listed in road_graph.managed_objects with a line geometry type, and have the fields road_code, start_marker_code, start_abscissa, end_marker_code and end_abscissa. The function road_graph.add_managed_objects_triggers() creates this trigger on the line tables with the column add_trigger_on_geom_change set to True. It is fired after the update of the geometry, so that the references of the updated line have already been calculated, for example by the trigger trg_calculate_managed_object_references. It is equivalent to:

CREATE TRIGGER trg_update_managed_object_linked_geometries
AFTER UPDATE OF geom
ON public.demo_painting
FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE PROCEDURE road_graph.update_managed_object_linked_geometries();

The connected lines are not modified when a line is split or merged with the Lizmap actions, when the managed objects are updated from the road graph, or when the editing session is merged.

docs.title: Update rules
docs.text:
When the user merges the data from the editing session, every impacted object is automatically updated based on the rule chosen by the administrator:

  • Point objects are often not moved, but their references must be updated, e.g. a road sign.
  • (Multi)linestring objects must often follow the changes: the start and end points are kept and only the nodes in between are edited, e.g. a painting roadwork.

To keep the merge fast on long roads, only the objects which may be impacted by the modifications are updated (see Impacts of the modifications on the references):

  • the objects located less than 50 m from the modified edges,
  • if the geometry of the road has changed, the objects located downstream of the first modified edge: up to the end of the road if the table has a cumulative field, or else up to the last marker of the modified edges,
  • the objects located between a modified marker and the previous marker.

An edge only split by a node, for example at a new crossroad, or whose attributes only have changed, does not change the geometry of the road. The other objects keep their references and geometries.

If the geometry of an object cannot be calculated from its references, for example when its end references are before its start references, the object is not updated and a warning is displayed, but the merge is not cancelled.

The algorithm Update managed objects from the road graph can also be run manually on a given layer, with the following parameters:

  • Update policy: Update geometries or Update references,
  • Update geometries - Preserve start & end points when updating line geometries: No or Yes.

docs.title: Example: impacts of a graph modification
docs.text:
The road D613 has two business objects:

  • a tree, in the table demo_trees with the update policy references, located at PR 43 + 450.53 m,
  • a safety barrier, in the table demo_safety_barriers with the update policy geometry, from PR 43 + 120 m to PR 45 + 18 m.

The road is realigned between the marker 43 and the tree: in an editing session, a vertex of the edge is moved 40 m away from the road axis. The edge, and therefore the road, becomes 46.71 m longer (from 563.30 m to 610.01 m).

When the editing session is merged, the two objects are updated according to their policy:

Object Update policy Before the merge After the merge Tree references PR 43 + 450.53 m PR 43 + 497.24 m: the tree has not moved, but it is now 46.71 m further from the marker 43 Safety barrier geometry PR 43 + 120 m to PR 45 + 18 m, 1,843.31 m long Same references. The geometry is calculated again and follows the new shape of the road: 1,889.57 m long
  • For the tree, a real object on the ground, the geometry is right and the references are updated.
  • For the safety barrier, the references are kept: its start and end points stay at the same places, since the markers have not moved, and the geometry between them follows the realigned road.

The updated objects are listed in the column last_updated_objects_ids of the managed_objects layer, and are displayed by the layer vm_managed_objects (see below).

docs.title: Last updated objects
docs.text:
The layer vm_managed_objects shows, for each managed table, the objects updated by the last merge of an editing session, as a 10m buffer around them. It is useful to have a quick look at the impacted objects.

This layer is a materialized view based on the view road_graph.v_managed_objects, which can be slow to compute. It is refreshed automatically at the end of the merge of an editing session. To refresh it manually, for example after running the algorithm Update managed objects from the road graph, use:

REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY road_graph.vm_managed_objects;

docs.text:
The plugin adds the provider RoadNetwork to the QGIS Processing toolbox (menu Processing / Toolbox). Most of the algorithms are also available with the buttons of the toolbar and panels.

Group Algorithm Usage Configuration Configure plugin Choose the PostgreSQL connection of the project Structure Create database structure Install the schema road_graph in the database Structure Upgrade database structure Upgrade the schema after a plugin upgrade Administration Create database local interface Create the QGIS administration project Editing Import data from template Fill an empty road graph from edges and markers layers Editing Clone data to a new editing session Copy the data of an editing session area into the sandbox Editing Merge editing session data Merge the sandbox data into the production data Editing Update managed objects from the road graph Calculate the references from the geometries, or the geometries from the references, of a layer Linear referencing Get road sections from a line (GPS track) Get the sections of the roads followed by lines, for example GPS tracks

All the algorithms have a parameter PostgreSQL connection to the database: by default, the connection chosen with the algorithm Configure plugin.

docs.title: Configure plugin
docs.text: Choose the PostgreSQL connection used by the current QGIS project. It must be run before the other algorithms. See Configure the plugin.

docs.title: Create database structure
docs.text: Install the schema road_graph, with its tables, views and functions, and the editing schema road_graph_editing. See Create the database structure.

docs.title: Upgrade database structure
docs.text: Upgrade the database structure to the version of the plugin, after a plugin upgrade. The administration panel shows if an upgrade is needed. See Upgrade database structure.

docs.title: Create database local interface
docs.text: Create a QGIS administration project with all the layers, styles, labels and actions. See Create your database local interface and Administration project.

docs.title: Import data from template
docs.text: Fill an empty road graph from an edges layer and a markers layer. The roads, nodes, edges and markers are created, and the references of the edges are calculated. See Import the road graph.

docs.title: Clone data to a new editing session
docs.text:
Copy the production data located inside the last editing session polygon with the status created into the editing schema road_graph_editing, the sandbox. The status of the session becomes cloned.

Also available with the toolbar button Clone data to the editing sandbox and with the action Create editing session of the editing_sessions layer.

The algorithm refuses to run if:

  • the editing_sessions layer is in editing mode: save the changes and stop the editing beforehand,
  • an editing session with the status edited has not been merged or dropped yet,
  • there is no editing session with the status created: draw the editing session polygon beforehand.

See Road graph editing.

docs.title: Merge editing session data
docs.text:
Merge the data of the editing session with the status edited into the production schema road_graph, update the managed objects impacted by the changes, then empty the sandbox and delete the merged editing session.

Also available with the toolbar button Merge editing sandbox data.

The algorithm refuses to run if the editing_sessions layer cannot be found or is in editing mode, or if there is no editing session with the status edited.

See Road graph editing.

docs.title: Update managed objects from the road graph
docs.text:
Update the references or the geometries of the features of a vector layer from the road graph. The layer can be a PostgreSQL table of the database, or any other vector layer, for example a GeoPackage layer.

Parameters:

  • Input vector layer: a point or (multi)linestring layer,
  • Update policy:
    • Update references: the references of each feature are calculated from its geometry,
    • Update geometries: the geometry of each feature is calculated from its references,
  • Update geometries - Preserve start & end points when updating line geometries: No or Yes. Used only to update the geometries of a line layer:
    • No: the geometry is calculated from the stored references,
    • Yes: the references are first calculated from the start and end points of the line, then the geometry is calculated from them. The line keeps its start and end points, and follows the road between them. Use it when the start and end points are right but the references are outdated or the line does not follow the road,
  • Output layer: the layer created with the updated features.

The input layer must have the reference fields corresponding to its geometry type:

  • point layers: road_code, marker_code, abscissa, and optionally offset, side and cumulative,
  • linestring layers: road_code, start_marker_code, start_abscissa, end_marker_code, end_abscissa, and optionally offset and side.

The algorithm supports the in-place editing of the input layer: select the layer, toggle its editing mode, then use the button Edit Features In-Place of the Processing toolbox. The features are then updated directly in the layer, and the changes can be checked before saving them.

For the tables registered in the managed_objects layer, the same updates can be done with SQL, see Calculate the references. They are also done automatically when an editing session is merged, see Update rules.

docs.title: Get road sections from a line (GPS track)
docs.text:
Get the sections of the roads followed by each line of a layer, for example GPS tracks imported from GPX files, with the start and end references of each road.

For each line, the algorithm:

  1. snaps the line on the road graph edges, without zigzags between close roads, with the database function road_graph.get_snapped_line_from_track,
  2. gets the ordered list of the roads followed by the snapped line, with the database function road_graph.get_road_sections_from_snapped_line.

See GPS tracks for the details of these functions.

Parameters:

  • Input line layer (GPS tracks): a line or multiline layer, in any coordinate reference system. For a GPX file, open its layer tracks,
  • Snap the lines on the road graph: checked by default. Uncheck it only if the lines already follow the road graph edges, for example the result of a previous snapping,
  • advanced parameters, used to snap the lines:
    • Distance between the points added to the line (m): 2 by default,
    • Maximum distance between the line and the roads (m): 25 by default. The points of the line further from any road are ignored,
    • Penalty applied each time the road changes: 100 by default. Increase it if the result still has zigzags between close roads,
  • advanced parameter Maximum distance between the snapped line and the edges (m): 1 by default,
  • Road sections: the output layer.

The output layer contains one feature per road section, in the coordinate reference system of the road graph. Its geometry is the part of the snapped line on this road, and its fields are the fields of the input line, followed by:

Field Description road_order Order of the section along the line, from 1 road_code Code of the road start_marker, start_abscissa References of the start of the section, e.g. 14 and 905.27 for PR 14 + 905.27 m start_cumulative Cumulative distance from the start of the road to the start of the section end_marker, end_abscissa References of the end of the section end_cumulative Cumulative distance from the start of the road to the end of the section direction downstream if the line follows the road direction, upstream otherwise length Length of the section in meters

If a field of the input layer has the same name as one of these fields, for example road_code, the field of the section is renamed with a suffix, e.g. road_code_2.

docs.title: Administration project
docs.text:
The algorithm Create database local interface creates a QGIS administration project with all the layers, styles, labels and actions needed to visualize and edit the road network.

The project contains the following groups of layers:

  • editing_sessions: the areas of the editing sessions (created, cloned, edited), see Road graph editing,
  • Editing: the layers of the editing session schema road_graph_editing,
  • Data: the production data
    • managed_objects: the list of business tables based on the road network, see Managed objects,
    • glossary_road_class and roads,
    • markers: reference points (PR) and virtual markers (PRV),
    • Topology: the nodes and edges, styled by road class,
  • baselayers: the background maps.

docs.text: The menu Plugins / RoadNetwork contains the actions Show/hide the tools dock, Show/hide the administration dock, and Open online help, which opens this documentation.

docs.title: Administration panel
docs.text:
The panel RoadNetwork is used by the administrator to install and configure the database:

  • the group Information shows the PostgreSQL connection used by the project, the versions of the plugin and of the database structure, and checks that they match. If the database structure is older than the plugin, it asks to run the algorithm Upgrade database structure,
  • the group Install and configure runs the algorithms Configure plugin, Create database structure, Create database local interface and Upgrade database structure,
  • the group Import runs the algorithm Import data from template.

See Processing algorithms for the description of these algorithms.

docs.title: Tools panel
docs.text:
The panel RoadNetwork tools shows the references of a point, and allows to find a point from references:

  • the group Localisation concerns the production data (schema road_graph),
  • the group Localisation (editing) concerns the data of the current editing session (schema road_graph_editing): during an editing session, the references can be different from the production ones,
  • the group Options contains the checkbox Get references on hover ?, which updates the references when the mouse moves over the map, see below.

Each Localisation group contains the fields Road, Marker, Abscissa, Cumulative, Offset and Side (left or right), filled with the references of the point clicked or hovered on the map.

To find a point from references, type the road, the marker, the abscissa and, optionally, the offset and the side, then click on Find or press Enter: the map is centered on the corresponding point, which flashes.

docs.title: Quick search
docs.text:
The QGIS locator search bar (CTRL+K) can be used to search a road or a position on a road. No prefix is needed: the RoadNetwork results are displayed in the RoadNetwork group.

Type the road code and, optionally, the marker code, the abscissa, the offset and the side, separated by spaces:

  • D40: highlights the whole road,
  • D40 1 151: centers the map on the point D40 PR 1 + 151m,
  • D40 1 151 3 left: same point, with an offset of 3m on the left side.

docs.title: Get references on map click
docs.text: The tool Get references under the cursor shows the references of the point under the mouse: road code, marker, abscissa, offset and side. It can be toggled with the plugin toolbar button or with the shortcut CTRL+SHIFT+K. Hovering over the map is supported.

docs.title: Layer actions
docs.text:

They are used when the user would like to modify the Road graph. See the corresponding documentation.

The layers of the road graph issues created by the algorithm Check the road graph also have actions, to fix an issue with a right click: see Fix an issue with a right click.

The Python code of these actions is stored in the plugin: the actions of the project only call it, for example plugins['roadnetwork'].run_action('drop_editing_session', ...).

docs.title: Présentation des concepts de l'extension
docs.text: L'extension RoadNetwork aide à gérer un réseau routier départemental topologique et à faire du référencement linéaire avec QGIS et PostGIS.

docs.title: Réseau routier
docs.text:
Chaque route :

  • a un identifiant, par exemple D907,
  • est composée d'une suite de tronçons ordonnés (lignes simples).

Des bornes sont positionnées le long des routes. Leur position est souvent mesurée avec un GPS (X,Y).

docs.title: Topologie
docs.text:
Le réseau routier est un graphe construit avec des tronçons et des nœuds :

  • chaque tronçon a un nœud de début et un nœud de fin,
  • un tronçon peut avoir un tronçon précédent et un tronçon suivant,
  • les tronçons qui se croisent sont coupés par un nœud (s'ils sont au même niveau).

docs.title: Position et références
docs.text:
Cette organisation simple en routes, tronçons et bornes permet de déterminer la position de tout objet à partir :

  • d'un code de route : D902,
  • d'un code de borne : 1,
  • d'une abscisse : 500m.

Vous pouvez aussi indiquer un décalage optionnel, par exemple 3m, et un côté, par exemple left.

Tout point situé à moins de 50m d'une route a des références : D902 PR 1 + 500m (3m left).

docs.title: Référencement linéaire
docs.text:
Chaque objet, point ou (multi)ligne, est défini par ses références calculées à partir du réseau routier :

  • Points : arbres, lampadaires, accidents de la route, etc.
  • Lignes : peintures, glissières de sécurité, travaux, etc.

Il faut pouvoir :

  • calculer les références à partir de la géométrie de l'objet,
  • créer une géométrie à partir de références données :
    • un point,
    • une multi-ligne entre deux références.

docs.title: Cas particuliers
docs.text:
Discontinuité : des tronçons peuvent avoir été supprimés (ou avoir changé de statut).

Les giratoires ont leur propre code de route, par exemple GIR D35-D80, et coupent les autres routes.

docs.title: Glossaire
docs.text: Concept Définition Graphe Graphe orienté composé d'un ensemble de tronçons et de nœuds, qui représente le réseau routier sous la forme d'un filaire de voies, correspondant à l'axe de la chaussée. Route Suite consécutive de tronçons formant une route / une voie (par exemple D115). Tronçon Portion de route. Un tronçon est un segment orienté reliant deux nœuds (ligne simple). Nœud Les nœuds représentent les sommets de début et de fin de chaque tronçon. Borne Point créé par le gestionnaire du réseau routier, matérialisé physiquement sur le terrain par des marques peintes associées aux bornes kilométriques. Borne virtuelle Point créé par l'administrateur SIG pour faciliter l'administration du graphe, en particulier le calcul du point de repère + abscisse. Point de repère (PR) Anciennement appelé point kilométrique (PK). Données métier ou thématiques Ensemble de données thématiques superposées au graphe et liées topologiquement à celui-ci. Il peut s'agir de données ponctuelles (par exemple la signalisation verticale) ou linéaires (par exemple le revêtement de chaussée).

docs.title: Fonctions utiles
docs.text:
Le schéma road_graph fournit des fonctions SQL utilisables directement dans vos requêtes, par exemple dans le panneau Explorateur de QGIS (clic droit sur la connexion PostgreSQL ou le schéma, puis Exécuter le SQL...), dans psql ou dans une couche virtuelle construite sur une requête PostgreSQL.

Les exemples ci-dessous utilisent le système de coordonnées EPSG:2154 et la route D613 des données de test du plugin : les valeurs peuvent être légèrement différentes dans votre base.

docs.title: Fonctions de référencement linéaire
docs.text: Fonction Usage get_reference_from_point Références d'un point get_road_point_from_reference Point correspondant à des références get_road_substring_from_references Ligne entre deux références get_spatial_road Géométrie d'une route entière, avec les cumuls comme mesures

docs.title: Obtenir les références d'un point
docs.text:
road_graph.get_reference_from_point(_point, _road_code, _use_cache) renvoie les références d'un point, sous la forme d'un objet JSON :

SELECT road_graph.get_reference_from_point(
    ST_SetSRID(ST_MakePoint(473136.24, 6895774.58), 2154)
);

{
    "road_code": "D613", "marker_code": 44, "abscissa": 154.50,
    "cumulative": 43063.50, "offset": 15.00, "side": "left"
}
  • _point : le point, dans le système de coordonnées du graphe routier,
  • _road_code (optionnel) : le code de la route à utiliser. S'il n'est pas fourni, la route la plus proche est utilisée. Renseignez-le pour choisir la route d'un point situé près d'une intersection,
  • _use_cache (optionnel, False par défaut) : utilisé en interne pour accélérer le calcul de nombreux points d'une même route.

La fonction renvoie NULL si aucune route n'est à moins de 50 m du point.

Exemple : obtenir les références de toutes les entités d'une couche de points, sans les enregistrer :

SELECT
    t.id,
    r.ref->>'road_code' AS road_code,
    (r.ref->>'marker_code')::integer AS marker_code,
    (r.ref->>'abscissa')::real AS abscissa
FROM managed.demo_trees AS t,
LATERAL (SELECT road_graph.get_reference_from_point(t.geom, t.road_code) AS ref) AS r;

docs.title: Obtenir un point à partir de références
docs.text:
road_graph.get_road_point_from_reference(_road_code, _marker_code, _abscissa, _offset, _side) renvoie le point correspondant aux références données, dans la clé geom d'un objet JSON (géométrie GeoJSON) :

SELECT road_graph.get_road_point_from_reference('D613', 44, 154.5, 15, 'left');

{
    "road_code": "D613", "marker_code": 44, "abscissa": 154.5, "offset": 15, "side": "left",
    "closest_marker_abscissa": 0,
    "geom": {"type": "Point", "coordinates": [473136.24, 6895774.58], "crs": {...}}
}
  • _offset : distance en mètres par rapport à l'axe de la route. Utilisez 0 pour un point sur la route,
  • _side : left ou right, dans le sens de la route.

Pour obtenir une géométrie PostGIS :

SELECT ST_GeomFromGeoJSON(
    road_graph.get_road_point_from_reference('D613', 44, 154.5, 15, 'left')->>'geom'
) AS geom;

docs.title: Obtenir une ligne entre deux références
docs.text:
road_graph.get_road_substring_from_references(_road_code, _start_marker_code, _start_marker_abscissa, _end_marker_code, _end_marker_abscissa, _offset, _side, _from_first_edge_start, _to_last_edge_end) renvoie la ligne de la route entre deux références, dans la clé geom d'un objet JSON :

-- Line of the road D613 between the references 44 + 100 m and 44 + 600 m
SELECT ST_Length(
    (road_graph.get_road_substring_from_references('D613', 44, 100, 44, 600, 0, 'right')->>'geom')::geometry
);
-- 500.00
  • le résultat est une MultiLineString : la route peut être composée de plusieurs parties, par exemple de part et d'autre d'un giratoire, qui a son propre code de route,
  • _offset et _side : pour décaler la ligne par rapport à l'axe de la route, par ex. 3 et left pour un marquage du côté gauche,
